544533|2026-03.headline: Seshaasai Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.6% YoY to INR 405 crore with EBITDA margin of 30.8%; FY26 revenue fell 1.5% to INR 1,441 crore, no FY27 guidance.
544533|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR 404-405 crore, up 8.1% QoQ and 9.6% YoY, led by communication and fulfilment and IoT. EBITDA was about INR 125 crore (30.8% margin, up 330 bps YoY) and PAT about INR 82 crore (20.2% margin, up 316 bps YoY), helped by lower finance costs after IPO debt repayment and interest income on IPO funds. For FY26, revenue declined 1.5% to INR 1,441 crore on a temporary moderation in Payment Solutions, while EBITDA reached INR 394 crore (27.4% margin) and PAT INR 240 crore (16.7% margin). Management declined to give FY27 guidance, deferring any update until after Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 398 crore, incl. ~INR 195 crore unutilised IPO funds

segments.name: Payment Solutions
segments.commentary: About 47.5% of Q4 revenue and ~50% of FY26 revenue; hit by PSU/private bank issuance moderation and low COVID-era renewal base. Added 21 new bank/fintech customers, lost none; won a multi-year PSU bank tender worth ~INR 8.7 crore. Metal cards are ~4% of the segment.

segments.name: Communication and Fulfilment Solutions
segments.commentary: 39% of FY26 revenue (39.8% of Q4) and grew 29% YoY; added ~8 customers. Management expects a marginal decline in FY27 but described the segment as stable.

segments.name: IoT Solutions
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue (12.4% of Q4), grew about 45-48% YoY (figures varied across the call). Added ~65 customers. RFID utilisation about 70% for FY26 and 80-85% in Q4. SIM division began material revenue in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue guidance by segment; management will revisit after Q1 FY27 given geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
No margin guidance for FY27/FY28; management expects product mix shift to IoT, eSIM and other solutions to support good margins.
IoT revenue expected to grow faster than the ~47% achieved in FY26.
eSIM commercial revenue expected from H2 FY27, after a compliance step due July/August 2026.
Capex of about INR 160-200 crore through FY27 across Payment Solutions and IoT, plus modernisation, partly funded from IPO proceeds.
Payment card business expected to bottom out, with renewal volumes to recover.
capex_capacity: Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities became operational in Q4 FY26; Nagpur and Bengaluru still under construction.
SIM capacity about 7 million per month, running at about 30% utilisation.
eSIM capacity of 2-3 million per month depending on form factor; commercial production not yet started.
RFID capacity utilisation about 70% for FY26 and 80-85% in Q4 FY26; three plants can do inlay manufacturing.
Bengaluru facility received GSMA SAS-UP certification for SIM/eSIM manufacturing and personalisation.
demand_pricing: Payment card demand weakened due to lower issuance from PSU and private banks, COVID-era renewal base effects, and tighter bank and fintech compliance.
Top 10 customers contributed about 62.8% of FY26 revenue; 96.6% of revenue came from existing customers.
Gross margin improved on 7-8% material cost savings from procurement consolidation and inventory planning; management said FX was an adverse factor in Q4.
Export revenue about INR 3 crore in FY26; international work is via partners, with some overseas fintech RFPs at evaluation stage.
Domestic payment scheme and global fintech RFPs for metal card variants still under evaluation.
Market share of payment cards in India was 31.6% in FY25 per industry analysts.

qa_highlights.question: Will rupee depreciation hurt gross margins going into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin gains came from sourcing savings of 7-8% on top raw material categories plus operating leverage. Q4 FX was adverse but mostly hit materials bought earlier, so the exposure is still to be watched.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital intensity rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built up to manage global supply risks in Q1 and Q4, and surplus IPO cash inflates the cash line. Receivables and inventory are said to be in line with the business, with monitoring under way.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 guidance by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management will wait until Q1 FY27 for better visibility on the macro and geopolitical situation before guiding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the eSIM timeline and SIM capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: SIM is at about 30% utilisation of 7 million per month capacity and already supplies a leading telecom player. eSIM commercial production is expected after a July/August compliance step, with revenue from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the payment card business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the business to bottom out, with renewal volumes recovering from the COVID-era base and growth from premiumisation, transit and state-government card programmes; metal cards were about 4% of the segment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for backward integration into chips or inlays?
qa_highlights.answer: Inlay equipment has been in place for about 2.5 years and three plants can make inlays. Management said local inlay making will improve margins once it reaches scale, but gave no margin quantification and parked chip integration for now.

risks_watch: Payment Solutions volume recovery depends on bank renewal cycles and regulatory conditions; the segment is about half of revenue.
Rupee depreciation, input cost inflation and supply-chain constraints could pressure gross margins; management said input prices are rising.
eSIM commercial launch depends on the July/August compliance step and integration work; SIM utilisation is only about 30%.
Working capital days have risen over two years; inventory and receivables are being monitored.
Top 10 customers are 62.8% of revenue, so concentration risk remains.
Unutilised IPO proceeds of about INR 195 crore are to be deployed in later periods.

544533|2026-06.headline: Seshaasai Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.1% YoY to INR 377 crore, but gross margin fell to 41.7% on war-linked input costs.
544533|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 377 crore, up 21.1% YoY but down 6.9% QoQ against a seasonally strong Q4. Cost of materials consumed rose to 58.34% (about 411 bps above the FY26 average), compressing gross margin to 41.7% from 44.5% a year earlier. EBITDA grew to INR 94 crore at a 25.1% margin (up 135 bps YoY), and PAT rose 63.8% YoY to INR 60 crore at a 16% margin. Management reiterated an 8-12% medium-term revenue growth target and guided to a stronger H2 on mix and operating leverage, without giving a numeric margin guide.

financial_highlights.change: about 411 bps above FY26 average of 54.23%

segments.name: Payment solutions
segments.commentary: 42% of Q1 revenue, growing about 5% YoY; premium metal cards cited as the main margin-accretive growth driver, with early export traction in Europe and Africa.

segments.name: Communication and fulfillment
segments.commentary: 40% of Q1 revenue, growing 13% YoY; management guides this segment to be roughly flat over the coming years, and it has the slightly lower EBITDA margin.

segments.name: IoT solutions
segments.commentary: 18% of Q1 revenue, growing 145% YoY; management expects about 45% growth in FY27 and 35-40% in FY28, with IoT at 15-18% of FY27 revenue.

Greenfield metal card facility in Bengaluru described as almost ready; certification and compliance expected to start by Q4, with operations before end of calendar 2026.
Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities still under construction.
SIM card business capacity utilisation about 40% in Q1.
IPO proceeds: INR 24.4 crore deployed in Q1 (capex INR 6.7 crore, GCP INR 13.7 crore, issue expenses INR 3.9 crore).
demand_pricing: Two multi-year PSU bank tenders won in Q1, about INR 73 crore revenue over the tenure.
Top 10 customers about 56% of revenue; more than 95% from existing clients.
Input cost pressure attributed to the war: management said 40-45% of the impact is currency and the rest is commodity, logistics and freight.
Working with customers on price revisions to protect margins.
Chip prices broadly flat in Q1 procurement; marginal INR-neutral improvement offset by USD appreciation; company built chip inventory, and supplier lead times have lengthened.
Insurance client count fell (life 13 to 10, general 9 to 7) but management said the churned clients were near-zero business and no business was lost to re-tender.
Telecom SIM work with a large (third-largest) operator: about 20% of its pre- and post-paid SIM requirement, targeting 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: How should we look at full-year revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 8-12% revenue growth for FY27 and declined to give EBITDA or PAT figures, promising quarterly disclosure of margin drivers instead.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin drop is operating leverage versus pricing and rupee, and can costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed 40-45% of the input cost impact to currency and the rest to war-driven commodity, logistics and freight costs; operating leverage should improve margins quarter on quarter if conditions do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical utilisation is 65-70%, peaking at 85-90%; capex stays at INR 140-160 crore per year and the Bengaluru metal card facility should be operational before end-2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for IoT, cards and communication?
qa_highlights.answer: IoT to grow about 45% in FY27 and 35-40% in FY28; communication and fulfilment flat; payment solutions around 10-12% CAGR, with IoT contributing 15-18% of revenue by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of UPI and MDR on card business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UPI's impact on card issuance has already played out, that UPI adoption is near saturation, and that volume forecasts factor in UPI.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Bengaluru facility contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hoping for some contribution this year, with meaningful contribution from FY28 onwards, but declined to quantify.

Payment solutions grew only about 5% YoY in Q1; the UPI and MDR debate could affect card volumes.
Bengaluru and Nagpur facility approvals and timelines.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 56% of revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: Some customers accepted price hikes; contracts up for renewal are being repriced. Management said input costs are largely outside its control and is focusing on product mix and lean operations.

544536|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations rose 28.7% to INR68.4 crores and PAT to INR38.3 crores, with Q4 PAT turning to INR10.5 crores from a loss.
544536|2026-03.overview: Wealth First reported FY26 consolidated revenue from operations of INR68.4 crores (up 28.7% from INR53.2 crores) and PAT of INR38.3 crores (vs INR34.1 crores). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR16.5 crores versus a loss of INR3.3 crores in Q4 FY25, helped by insurance sales, ARR asset flows and no MTM drag after the trading book was taken to zero. Management framed FY26 as a transition year: AMC licence received, insurance broking licence obtained, and the equity trading book exited. Cost-to-income rose to 29.9% (ex one-offs) from 23%, which management attributed to strategic and growth investments.

544537|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR3,337 crore and EBITDA rose 27% QoQ to INR138 crore, but margin stayed thin at 4.2%.
544537|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was about INR3,337 crore, up 58% YoY and 22% QoQ, with H1 revenue of about INR6,061 crore. EBITDA was about INR138 crore (4.2% margin) versus INR109 crore (4.0%) in Q1, and PAT rose about 30% QoQ to INR90 crore. Copper volumes drove growth, with the new copper anode plant contributing its first sales, while working capital days fell to 49 from 66 at FY26-end and net debt/equity improved to about 0.5x from 0.7x. Management said margins may moderate as copper mix shifts, and most expansion items (cathode, wire rod, busbar, antimony, plastic) are slated for Q3 or Q4 FY27, with Kuwait delayed by West Asia logistics.

Copper including the new initiative was 8% of revenue, while management also said copper is over 65% of turnover.

segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 34,851 MT, up from about 32,150 MT in Q1 but below year-ago levels. EBITDA rose to INR67 crore from INR60 crore, and EBITDA per ton to INR19,310 from INR18,660. Management said lead is about 30% of turnover.

segments.name: Aluminium and aluminium alloys
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 2,493 MT, up from 2,201 MT in Q1. Segment EBITDA rose to INR5.3 crore from INR4.7 crore.

segments.commentary: Both 800 MT/month anode phases commissioned (1,600 MT/month total), Phase II in trial run. H1 FY27 value-added sales about 3,575 MT. Management cited about INR14,434 per ton of separate EBITDA for this business, which is expected to rise with utilisation.

segments.name: Jain CY Circular Solutions (Ahmedabad subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Commenced commercial operations and booked about INR25.4 crore of revenue in Q2. Input capacity is about 71,000 MT/year of scrap, with output of about 25,000 MT/year of copper products at full ramp.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of more than 30% (30-40% range cited) for FY27, subject to market conditions and execution; management cited a 10-year average of about 40% CAGR.
Copper EBITDA per ton expected to keep rising with value-added products, per Kamlesh Jain, though management also flagged likely EBITDA margin moderation as copper mix scales.
Cathode Phase I (750 MT/month) commissioning imminent; Phase II targeted Q4 FY27. Wire rod (600 MT/month) and busbar and profiles (1,500 MT/month) targeted Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle expected to range 50-70 days going forward, with quarterly swings of 10-20 days.
Management said FY27 volumes should rise, but declined to give segment-wise volume guidance on the call and will share it by email.

capex_capacity: Copper anode plant: Phase I and II each 800 MT/month, total 1,600 MT/month installed; Phase II in trial run.

Copper cathode plant: 1,500 MT/month total in two 750 MT/month phases. Phase I civil work complete and commissioning at an advanced stage; Phase II targeted Q4 FY27. Phase I capex about INR120 crore (value-added copper total, about 60% of total capex attributed to cathode), Phase II expected to be lower.
Copper wire rod (600 MT/month) and busbar and profiles (1,500 MT/month) targeted for Q3 FY27.

Antimony recovery facility about 100 MT/month targeted Q3 FY27; dedicated plastic recycling plant capex about INR15 crore, operations targeted Q3 FY27 (management said early production has started at the shed).

Kuwait facility: machinery fully manufactured but shipment delayed by West Asia war and lack of specialised containers; management expects shipment within about 30 days and gave no firm execution timeline. It is intended as a lead ingot sourcing point.
demand_pricing: Sourcing shifted toward domestic: management said domestic share of total purchases is about 38-39% across metals, and local sourcing now exceeds 50-60% per Kamlesh Jain. Domestic scrap prices track LME and landed cost, so there is no direct cost benefit; the benefit is lower working capital.

Lead sourcing is challenged by shipping disruption and high freight from the Middle East. Management is offsetting with local purchases and new sourcing areas, and expects to manage Q3 without problems.
Management said raw material for the next four months is secured and expects no sourcing problem this fiscal year. Lead volumes rose about 8% QoQ.
Management said RCM on e-waste scrap will help only marginally unless GST on scrap purchases is reduced.

Competition: management positioned JRRL as a diversified multi-metal player (copper over 65% of turnover) versus lead-focused peers Gravita and POCL, and said the three cannot be compared like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the copper cathode plant and is Phase II similar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR120 crore covers the entire value-added copper capex (land, building, power, machines), with cathode about 60% of it. Phase II is lower, roughly 25-30% less per Mayank Pareek.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital fallen and has sourcing changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain attributed the decline to internal cash accumulation and a shift to local sourcing (now over 50-60%), which avoids pre-paid overseas purchases that tie up about two months of cash in transit.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic sourcing share has been flat at about 38-39%, and when will lead volumes return to 45,000-50,000 MT per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Hemant Jain said domestic sourcing is about 38-39% of total purchases across all metals. Kamlesh Jain said lead volumes rose about 8% QoQ but fell YoY, and gave no date for returning to the 45,000-50,000 MT run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will copper EBITDA per ton keep rising, and what is the value-add per stage?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain said copper EBITDA per ton rose from INR30,000 to about INR37,500 and should keep rising. Mayank Pareek said cathode adds 1-1.5% to the bottom line, wire rod another 1-1.5%, and the average uplift across the chain is 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain said revenue growth of more than 30% (around 30-40%) is expected for FY27, subject to market conditions, and gave no margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why do the MTM figures differ between other income and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Hemant Jain said other income includes MTM on open options, while the figure in COGS includes expired options and open futures tied to inventory or sales hedges. He offered to send a detailed reconciliation by email.

544540|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 35% to INR1,525 crore and PAT 56%, but Q4 margin fell 70-80 bps on steel prices; FY27 guided to 30% Prefab growth.
544540|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as its first full year as a listed company, with revenue up 35% to INR1,525 crore, PAT up 56%, and about INR107-108 crore of debt repaid. Free operating cash flow was about INR135 crore, roughly 85% of EBITDA. Q4 margins fell 70-80 bps to about 9.7-10% because steel prices spiked after minimum import price and anti-dumping duties, and management says most customers (80%+ of contracts) have accepted price increases. Management guided FY27 Prefab growth of 30% (revenue INR1,920-1,950 crore), an order book target of INR2,000 crore plus, and margins of 10%+ / 10.5% plus.

term loans of about INR70 crore plus working capital loans

financial_highlights.change: expected to fall 20-25 bps in FY27

segments.commentary: FY26 PEB revenue about INR1,382 crore per analyst tally (confirmed by management); FY27 guided to 30% growth to INR1,925-1,950 crore. Margin guided at 10-10.5%, with packaging about 100 bps higher.

Gujarat (Vithlapur) greenfield: first phase about 50,000 MT PEB; capex about INR100-110 crore (about INR38 crore land spent, INR60-65 crore balance); commissioning by end Q4 FY27, meaningful utilisation from FY28.
Q4 FY26 utilisation 83% (up from 58% in Q1, 77% in Q2, 67% in Q3); management says 70-75% is a strong quarterly level, peak about 83-84%.

demand_pricing: Order book INR1,117-1,127 crore, giving visibility of about 6-8 months; management says 100% should execute within FY27 (5-10% at risk from EC or funding delays).

Steel price spike in March 2026 driven by minimum import price and anti-dumping duties; price increases obtained from most customers, but not 100% pass-through.
Competition: three to four large players; management says margin cannot be commanded on differentiation, so growth and utilisation are prioritised.
West India share of order book fell from about 30% (FY25) to 17-18% (FY26); Gujarat plant to address this.

qa_highlights.question: Is management chasing growth by adding capacity ahead of confirmed orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is being added against demand; past South capacity was absorbed within 18 months, and Gujarat is expected to follow the same pattern.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins face pressure in FY27 and from steel costs in Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins guided at 10%+ for FY27; Q1 may see a little impact, Q2 not major. Price increases were secured on 80%+ of contracts, and about 32,000 tons of inventory bought at older prices covers Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue target and margin guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Prefab revenue target INR1,920-1,950 crore (30% growth); margins 10%+, with no margin expansion expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book executable in FY27 and what is the order inflow run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full INR1,100 crore should be executed this year, with 5-10% at risk. Order target is INR2,000 crore plus; monthly run rate was not given because project inflow is lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sandwich panel line be utilised and at what margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Mambattu utilisation targeted at 75-80%; the line adds about INR70-90 crore revenue and carries margins slightly above structural steel. Order book of 4 lakh sq m is about 75% captive and 25% external.

qa_highlights.question: Why is West revenue share falling and is market share being lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share is not lost; South capacity drove the mix. West freight is currently subsidised, and a Gujarat plant is expected to lift West share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Gujarat unit economics and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak revenue INR500-600 crore on 50,000 MT; capex INR100-110 crore, funded from IPO proceeds and cash on hand. Ramp-up takes time.

544540|2026-06.headline: EPACK Prefab Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~25% to INR366 crore, with EBITDA margin down ~100 bps to 9.4% on steel costs and order book at INR1,380 crore.
544540|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 25% YoY to INR366 crore from INR295 crore, and EBITDA rose to nearly INR35 crore from INR30.9 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 9.4% from 10.5%, which management attributed to steel price increases linked to the Middle East conflict, partly offset by fixed-price contract repricing and purchasing policy. Order inflow was INR580 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier, and the order book stood at about INR1,376-1,380 crore as of 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore (about 30% growth) and a 10.5-11.5% EBITDA margin from Q2 onwards, and announced a data center subsidiary with INR75 crore planned equity.

qa_highlights.question: Share of fixed-price vs pass-through orders in the current book?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are fixed-price; management manages risk by booking orders weekly at current prices. Steel rose 12-15% but the balance-sheet impact was about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 10-11% and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement from Q2 and full-year EBITDA margin of ~10.5%. Q1 dip was ~100 bps against an earlier estimate of ~200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Data center revenue potential, working capital, and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify until end-Q1 numbers are available and said the funding plan is undecided, with any debt expected to be modest.

qa_highlights.question: Sandwich panel order book fell from 4 lakh to 3.2 lakh sq m QoQ; is utilisation still rising?

qa_highlights.question: Win rate of ~20%: what drives the rate and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it bids on 30-40% of quotes and selects projects, and losses come partly from capacity constraints by region. A 20% win rate is said to be strong against 10-12% peers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company sustain 30% growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India fabrication demand of 12-19% of steel output, ~36 million tonnes by 2030 in the pessimistic case, and suggested EPACK's 0.3-0.35 million tonnes is a small share.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 10.5-11.5% from Q2 depends on repricing and new orders at post-war steel prices; Q1 margin was 9.4% and management said the impact was about 100 bps versus an earlier estimate of about 200 bps.
Most orders are fixed-price with no pass-through; steel rose 12-15% since the war began. Booking weekly at current prices is the main protection, so a further steel spike could hit margins again.

Capacity ramp-up timing: Ghiloth sandwich panel line due end-Q1 with production from Q2, Mambattu second AP line from Q2, Gujarat (~50,000 tpa) in Q4 FY27 with production from April 2027. Monsoon-related civil works delays were flagged as a Q2 execution risk.

Order book coverage: opening book INR1,110 crore on 1 April 2026 and order book INR1,376-1,380 crore at 30 June 2026 against FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore; FY27 order inflow target of INR2,000 crore, with INR580 crore booked in Q1 and management expecting more than 50% in H1. Win rate of about 20% and the sandwich panel order book (3.2 lakh sq m Mambattu line) need to be tracked.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Three of four Sumitomo JV CBG plants (20 TPD each, INR330 crore) are near commissioning for Q3, and about 72 TPD comes online from Q4; ethanol capacity stays at ~55 crore litres with no new ethanol capex, and the 15 crore litre court-ordered capacity has no timeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation is ~60% and rising to 80-90% (90-95% if the court capacity is implemented); orders on hand cover ~44 crore litres for FY27 against a Q2 plan of 11-12 crore litres, though Q2 depends on 5 crore litres of unlifted private OMC stock.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no further ethanol capex is planned and utilisation is only ~60%, so the high-utilisation trigger does not apply; CBG and SAF capex are already committed (INR760 crore CBG, INR2,000 crore SAF with EPC tender pending).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: FY29 (SAF); CBG revenue from Q4 FY27

rows.label: INR15 crore spillover payment from OMCs

rows.label: De-leveraging plan and pledged share release
rows.why: Finance cost is ~INR180 crore a year (7% of revenue vs 12.4% last quarter) and the debt-equity ratio is 0.59; management promised a plan and expects SBI/IREDA pledged-share release this quarter, but gave no details.

544545|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 606% YoY to INR811 crore and PAT turned to INR35 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.03% on maize prices up 25-30%.
544545|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR811 crore versus INR115 crore a year earlier, and up from INR627 crore in Q1, with PAT of about INR35 crore against a loss of INR38 crore. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.03% from a higher H1 level of about 18.2%, as maize prices rose 25-30% during the quarter and raw material was bought at elevated cost. Ethanol allocations were increased during the quarter after a Supreme Court judgment, lifting the last supply year's allocation from 24.5 crore litres to 34.5 crore litres, with a further 5 crore litres reported. Management guided to a shrinking bottom line in the coming year due to El Nino-linked feedstock shortages, while CBG capacity is being added.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Ethanol volumes sold were 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres in H1). About 8.5 crore litres of orders remain to be supplied in October-November, and management expects 6-7 crore litres of additional volume in November-December.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas)
segments.commentary: First 20 TPD JV plant with Sumitomo is ramping up; two more plants are expected in the quarter, taking installed capacity to about 72 TPD from four operating plants. Management expects about INR20 crore of CBG revenue from the two to three plants over the next two quarters.

segments.name: SAF (sustainable aviation fuel)
segments.commentary: Front-end engineering is ongoing and about INR150 crore of viability gap funding has been received under PM JI-VAN for the proposed plant. Capex awaits a government roadmap that has not yet been announced.

segments.name: Fuel retail
segments.commentary: About 7 outlets are operational with more nearing commissioning; outlet expansion is being slowed due to crude price volatility.

guidance_outlook: Ethanol capacity utilisation expected to rise to at least 75-80% on average, from 65-70% in the last supply year; new-year allocation expected at about 40-42 crore litres (one analyst question cited 45 crore litres as the expectation).

Ethanol EBITDA margin expected to dip about 1-2 percentage points on average versus the run-rate once new tenders are allocated; Q2 described as the seasonally weakest quarter, with margin recovery expected from Q3.
Management expects the bottom line to shrink due to El Nino-linked raw material price and availability pressure; intends to forward-buy and stock maize and rice.
Raw material cost as a share of revenue expected to be sub-70% going forward, versus 62-66% historically.
Ethanol gross margin currently about 30% per CFO, which management declined to guide forward.

CBG: expected capex of about INR300 crore for four to five add-on plants at about INR65 crore per plant, with incremental term debt of about INR70-80 crore; GOBARdhan subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD (25% currently receivable) and about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

Badami (Unit 5) slump sale expected to realise about INR170 crore, with about INR125-130 crore of term loan repaid and about INR40-46 crore retained; management expects about INR22 crore annual cost savings.
capex_capacity: Ethanol installed capacity about 2,000 KLPD (about 1,900 crore litres per year industry view); management says all ethanol capex is complete and no ethanol capex is planned next quarter. Three plants converted to grain-based dual feed; one 400 KLPD plant to run on C-heavy molasses/ENA.
Ethanol capacity utilisation was 62% in Q2 at the 400 KLPD plant and about 64-65% in H1.
CBG installed capacity to reach about 72 TPD by end of quarter; plan to start construction of six additional units with GAIL.
Srikakulam SAF plant planned on the PM JI-VAN grant; capex to start only after the government roadmap is announced.
Expected Q3 CBG working capital requirement of about INR25-30 crore at 100 TPD scale; current 10 TPD plant needs about INR2.5-3 crore.
demand_pricing: Maize prices rose 25-30% in Q2; management expects maize availability down about 35% and rice and sugarcane down 10-12% next year due to El Nino.
Ethanol realisation this year: maize-based about INR68/litre, damaged food grain about INR64, FCI rice about INR60; blended average about INR64-65 versus about INR67 last year.
Government reduced maize-based ethanol price by about INR3/litre in the current tender; sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses banned for the 2026-27 supply year.
ENA long-contract prices about INR62-63/litre, with ENA production cost about INR1.5-2/litre lower than ethanol from C-heavy molasses.
DDGS byproduct price about INR26-30/kg. CBG revenue per TPD about INR4-4.5 crore; gas price rises from INR84 to about INR104/kg (up to INR116-120/kg for higher purity) under GOBARdhan 2.0.
Management sees roughly 230 mono-feed sugar-based plants out of about 500 unable to supply continuous ethanol, and the OMC tender demand about 1,100 crore litres.

Chemical/industrial alcohol demand cited at 250-300 crore litres; management expects 40-50% to be met by Indian producers. Industrial alcohol imports (RS) now INR58-60/litre versus INR47-48 previously.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance for next two quarters, and what execution risks for the Srikakulam SAF plant and feedstock strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8.5 crore litres of existing orders for October-November; new-year allocation expected at 40-42 crore litres, subject to bids. Feedstock to be sourced nationally (Bihar, MP, Punjab) with warehouses being secured.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans, and working capital risk from CBG expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No ethanol capex; CBG capex about INR300 crore for four to five plants with about INR70-80 crore new term debt. Working capital need is minimal; CBG subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD reduces term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol volumes this quarter, and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol sold: 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres H1). Margin expected to rise from Q3 with a possible 1-2 point average dip once tenders are allocated.

qa_highlights.question: CBG revenue ramp and subsidy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore CBG revenue expected over the next two quarters from two to three plants; subsidy of about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and raw material cost structure for ethanol and CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize ethanol about INR68/litre, blended about INR64-65; raw material share below 70% of revenue. CBG EBITDA guided at about 50-55% at 20 TPD, against a track record near 60%; revenue about INR80 crore per 20 TPD plant.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory holding and margin sustainability in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of INR206 crore at September is expected to clear with the new season. Management would not disclose the maize-based realisation for next year before allocations; about 4.5 crore litres remain to be supplied this quarter.

risks_watch: Maize and raw material price inflation and feedstock availability with El Nino; management expects a squeeze on the bottom line in the next supply year.
Ethanol price cut in the current OMC tender (about INR3/litre) and allocation outcome for 40-42 crore litres, not yet confirmed.
SAF project depends on an unannounced government roadmap; no capex has started.
Finance costs rose to INR87 crore in H1 (from INR76 crore), and debt-to-equity is about 0.55x; new CBG term debt of about INR70-80 crore is planned.
Promoter pledge and share purchase intent (stake about 71%, headroom to 75%) and a personal loan were raised in the call; management said it does not affect the company.
Subsidy receipt timing (INR25-30 crore expected by December or January) and the Badami slump sale completion.

Management was evasive on forward ethanol margin and realisation numbers, saying these depend on allocations, and it deflected a question on promoter personal financing.

544546|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 42.5% to INR84.22 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 17% and PAT margin to 10.9% as spending on talent, platform and new verticals rose.
544546|2026-03.overview: Chatterbox Technologies held its maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), its first since its IPO. Revenue from operations grew 42.5% YoY to INR84.22 crores, and EBITDA and PAT rose in absolute terms to INR14.32 crores and INR9.2 crores. Margins moderated, which management attributed to investment in talent, platform capabilities and new verticals. Management declined to give formal guidance, though it said FY27 net margins would be similar to FY26 with an aim to expand them. Several questions focused on the sharp fall in market cap after listing, the possibility of a QYOU Media merger, the delayed results timeline, and the AAGE edutainment app; management answered most of these qualitatively or deferred them.

segments.name: Chatterbox Represent (exclusive talent management)
segments.commentary: Contributed 39.27% of FY26 revenue, the largest vertical. Management said margins are fixed but absolute contribution can grow as exclusive creators are added; it manages over 100 creators exclusively.

segments.name: Brand Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 36.18% of FY26 revenue. No separate growth or margin commentary was given in the call.

segments.name: ChtrSocial
segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

guidance_outlook: No formal financial guidance given. Management said the opportunity ahead is significantly larger and it remains optimistic on healthy medium- to long-term growth.
FY27 net margin expected to be similar to FY26 (about 10%); management said it is aiming higher and streamlining opex.
ChtrSocial expected to at least double its revenue in the upcoming period; no percentage target given.
AAGE edutainment app launch targeted within FY27 after development was paused for the IPO; it is still at the UX/UI stage with focus-group validation planned.
Management said integrated benefits from QYOU Media collaboration will become more visible in H2 2026.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets roughly doubled, while intangible assets under development stayed at INR4.68 crores; the AAGE app was on hold during the IPO and is being resumed.
Chtr Studios (video production) and Dubai subsidiary were established; the Dubai subsidiary is not 100% owned by Chatterbox (reason asked but not clearly answered in the call).
No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management said growth came from a mix of higher ticket sizes, organic growth across verticals, new client wins and international expansion, with an equal-mix view endorsed by the analyst.
Over 500 brands served, more than 2,000 campaigns executed, and a team of over 100 professionals, per management.
Management does not disclose net revenue retention, but said a significant part of growth came from existing enterprise clients with larger mandates and cross-selling of ChtrSocial and Studios.
Creator economy said to grow at a 25-30% CAGR globally, and BCG estimate cited of over USD 1 trillion annual creator-economy spend by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals will drive growth over the next 2-3 years, and will ChtrSocial, Represent, international or technology lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come from multiple engines: ChtrSocial, technology/AI platform, exclusive talent management and international (MENA first, then APAC and LATAM). No percentage targets were given.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments have the highest margins and where is operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Farrel Arora said ChtrSocial and the production arm (Studios) have the highest margin contribution. Represent is scalable in absolute rupee terms but its margins are fixed.

qa_highlights.question: Why has intangible assets under development stayed flat at INR4.68 crores, and what is the AAGE app?
qa_highlights.answer: AAGE was put on hold during the IPO. It is an edutainment app mixing short-form video, learning and gamification with AI; launch is targeted within FY27 after UX/UI curation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR26 crore trade receivables is not yet due?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR17.5 crores is within the standard 60-day credit period. Management said collections usually realise in 60-90 days (around 70-75 days on average), and most of the not-due amount should now be realised.

qa_highlights.question: Did volume growth come from more campaigns, new clients or deeper wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix of all three, with deeper wallet share from existing clients and international efforts contributing; no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the reasons behind the Dubai subsidiary not being 100% owned, the top-five customers, and whether QYOU Media will merge with Chatterbox at a market cap of INR78 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Curt Marvis declined to comment on any merger, saying only that the company is always looking at ways to increase shareholder value and that a public vehicle enables accretive M&A. Top-five customer data and the Dubai ownership reason were not answered directly in the call.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin 17% and PAT margin 10.9% in FY26, with FY27 PAT margin guided at similar levels (about 10%). Watch whether opex is streamlined.
Receivables: INR26 crores of trade receivables at March 2026 against INR84.22 crores revenue. Track receivable days and cash conversion next quarter.
Results disclosure timing: results were announced on 29 May, with the investor presentation and call later, and a family matter was cited as the cause. Investor-relations sentiment was questioned.

Related-party and governance questions: the parent QYOU Media (listed in Canada/US) merger was raised but not addressed; the Dubai subsidiary ownership and the market-cap decline post-listing (analyst cited about INR78 crores vs about INR160 crores at debut) remain open.
Customer concentration: top-five customer contribution was asked for but not disclosed.
AAGE app launch in FY27 and its monetisation are unproven; management said it will validate the model first.

544547|2026-03.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.
544547|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly standalone and consolidated revenue in company history, with standalone revenue up 89% YoY to INR133 crore and consolidated at INR192 crore. Full-year standalone revenue grew 48% to INR313 crore, but standalone PAT was INR12.44 crore and consolidated PAT was INR12.76 crore, with management attributing the margin pressure to freight and geopolitical logistics costs, HexL brand investment and higher employee costs. Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

segments.commentary: Customised machines of other brands contributed about 62%, refurbished used construction equipment about 35%, and HexL own-brand about 5% (4.9-5% consolidated; about 7% standalone).

segments.name: Geography FY26
segments.commentary: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each (per management's approximate figures), with the rest in single digits. Management said exports are about 97-98% of revenue.

segments.name: HexL brand
segments.commentary: Own brand in early build-out with lower margins; management targets 11-12% of FY27 revenue and about 150 units in FY27.

Management expects FY27 profitability to improve faster than revenue if Middle East logistics normalise.
Long-run margin targets: 12-14% PAT for HexL and refurbished used equipment; 2-4% for new equipment of other brands.

Cash conversion cycle expected to improve next year, not in the near term.

No immediate plans for new overseas geographies or inventory hubs, though 80-100 countries are cited as the long-term addressable base.
Management did not disclose a new manufacturing unit or specific capex plan.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for construction and mining equipment stayed resilient, supported by infrastructure, industrial capex and replacement demand in emerging markets.
West Asia crisis raised logistics costs, freight, insurance and currency volatility; management said freight costs were absorbed in P&L and were the main reason for profit decline.
Mexico Q4 performance was better than Q3, but management did not quantify FY26 Mexico decline.
South Africa emerged as a strong contributor to offset moderation in other markets.
No order pipeline; inventory-led sales model with working capital churn of 2-2.5 times.

qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised scale to INR600-800 crore revenue at about 5-7% consolidated PAT, and said cash conversion cycle would stay elevated while HexL is built.

qa_highlights.question: How will HexL affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory positioning and customer credit for HexL keep the cash conversion cycle higher; management expects it to ease after the brand is established, next year at the earliest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the geographic mix and how is Mexico trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each; management said Mexico Q4 was stronger than Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital requirement for further growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is INR300-350 crore; management said each INR100 crore of additional working capital could support roughly INR200-300 crore of revenue after the INR600-700 crore milestone.

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.
544547|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores and consolidated revenue grew 15.9% to INR56.57 crores. Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. Management said inventory of about INR96.8 crores, mostly overseas, is being built as part of the international strategy, and that investments in people and systems will weigh on margins for several quarters.

segments.commentary: Management said it is in early stages, with heavy spending on marketing, discounting and dealer development. Management cited a long-term PAT target of 12% to 14% (also 12% to 15% in an earlier call) and a 20% to 40% retail price advantage versus global brands.

segments.name: New/customised equipment, used and refurbished equipment
segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

Management expects healthier profitability in 2 to 3 years once shipping, interest and manpower costs settle; near-term profit is being sacrificed for long-term build-out.
Inventory expected to stay at similar levels, plus or minus a few percentage points, in lower double digits, with conversion over about 2 quarters.

Post-IPO capital base and enhanced banking facilities cited as capacity to support higher volumes.
demand_pricing: Africa is now a major market; management said the Middle East revenue gap was partly filled by Africa.
Freight and shipping costs rose on geopolitical route closures and longer shipping times, which also lengthened debtor cycles.
Commodity inflation is not expected to be fully passed through; costs are partly absorbed and partly passed to suppliers and customers.
Management said new customised equipment is in highest demand, driven by faster availability and lower breakdown times for end users.
Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects results in 3 to 6 quarters. In 2 to 3 years it targets INR600 crores to INR700 crores revenue with healthier profitability, a dominant international business, and roughly equal revenue from the three verticals.

Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave no segment-level margin or revenue numbers.

Management said the company manufactures backhoe loaders under contract in China, and an analyst raised natural calamities there as a supply risk; management said the locations it uses are unaffected.

544550|2026-03.headline: Pace Digitek Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 60.5% YoY to Rs.1,097 crore; FY26 PAT Rs.307 crore (+10.1%), FY27 revenue guided Rs.3,200-3,400 crore.
544550|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.1,097 crore versus Rs.683 crore a year earlier, driven by project execution. Full-year revenue grew 8.3% to Rs.2,641 crore and PAT rose 10.1% to Rs.307 crore, but full-year EBITDA fell to Rs.455 crore from Rs.482 crore as the mix shifted from telecom to energy. Working capital absorbed cash: inventory was built to Rs.540 crore and trade receivables reached Rs.2,442 crore, which management expects to ease by September 2026. BESS manufacturing capacity is being raised from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026).

544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
544550|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

544557|2026-09.headline: Glottis Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 28.8% YoY to Rs 2,765 million, with EBITDA-level margin of about 1.2% (profit Rs 34 million).
544557|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was Rs 2,765 million, up 28.8% YoY and 17.9% QoQ, with other income of Rs 19 million and total income of Rs 2,783 million. Management said exports grew 344.4% YoY and now contribute about 42% of revenue, while logistics fell to about 50% share of revenue from 81%. Margin pressure from operating costs persisted, with profit of Rs 34 million at a 1.2% margin, and top-5 customer concentration fell to about 33% from 41%. The call was largely qualitative; several figures in the transcript are garbled by transcription and were not verified.

Management cited pressure on margins from operating costs
Export revenue up 344.4% YoY; was about 12% a year earlier

segments.commentary: Export revenue grew 344.4% YoY and contributed about 42% of total revenue, up from about 12% a year earlier. Management said it is focusing more on export business alongside import operations.

segments.name: Logistics (import-led)
segments.commentary: Logistics share of revenue moderated to about 50% from 81% in the year-ago quarter; import revenue reportedly grew 16.9% YoY. Share figures in the transcript are partly inconsistent.

segments.name: Home appliances
segments.commentary: Home appliances accounted for about 18% of revenue versus 11% a year earlier.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Renewable energy share fell to about 16% of revenue from 46% a year earlier, per management.

segments.name: Chemicals and automobiles
segments.commentary: Chemicals contributed about 7% and automobiles about 5% of revenue, with revenue up 532% and 110% YoY respectively. Engineering products about 10%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Asia contributed about 80% of revenue in Q2 FY27, North America about 11%, and the balance South America, Australia and other markets.

guidance_outlook: Management said it is very bullish on revenue growth and expects growth to be strong, with a reference to a 'double' (likely double-digit) growth, though no specific figure was given for FY27 or FY28.
Management said the challenge is sustaining and increasing bottom-line profitability, and that measures are being worked on.
Management expects crude-linked cost relief if crude settles near USD 70-80/bbl, citing a positive trend for profitability over the next two quarters; no quantified EBITDA guidance.
Container deployment expected to start from Q3 FY27; capex programme targeted to complete during FY27.

Warehousing and transportation margins expected to be double-digit, per management; subsidiaries in the US and Malaysia expected to contribute from around Q4 FY27 (Malaysia after property completion in Q3 or Q4).
capex_capacity: Fleet of about 85 vehicles post-deployment, with GPS tracking; plans to deploy vehicles in multiple locations.
Container deployment delayed due to raw material and geopolitical issues; production complete, rollout from Q3 FY27.
Long-term warehousing lease of about 200,000 sq ft, with plans to scale in South and West India.
Plans for more trucks/fleet deployment in different areas; a transport management system with real-time tracking is being developed. Investment amount not disclosed.
Subsidiaries: US subsidiary incorporated in March, operations started last month; Malaysia subsidiary (Glottis Logistics SDN BHD) just incorporated.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide pricing pressure from renewable energy and smaller regional players, per management.
Shipping lines are not offering long-term contracts due to crude volatility and charter availability; shippers and exporters are moving to spot pricing.
Air freight described as more profitable; management expects double-digit QoQ growth in air freight and has added sales teams and branches across India.
Freight rates reportedly up 4-5 times, prompting management to support customers while tightening customer selection.
Trade receivable days around one year per management's answer (figure as transcribed, may be garbled); measures underway to reduce receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Will falling crude prices lift EBITDA and guidance over the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude is settling and a positive trend is expected; it cited USD 70-80/bbl as a level that would help the industry. No quantified guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition shaping up, especially pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the whole industry faces similar pressure, with renewables declining and exports growing, and the company is focusing on verticals with more opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers committing to long-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: No; shipping lines are unwilling to sign long-term contracts given crude volatility and charter availability, so business is spot-driven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27/FY28 guidance for revenue growth and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is bullish on revenue growth, expects double-digit growth, and the focus is on sustaining and improving the bottom line; no margin figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter funding: is it short-term and reversible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said promoter funds of about Rs 60 crore (interest at 10%, tenure of 5 years) were taken to support working capital from high freight rates and expansion; it can be partly or fully repaid based on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Container fleet, utilisation and backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet is about 85 vehicles; containers to roll out from Q3 FY27 after delays from raw material and geopolitical issues; backward integration expected to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: Air freight growth ambitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Air freight is more profitable; management expects double-digit QoQ growth with new sales teams and branches.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of US tariffs and India-US trade deal on US-bound volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a vague answer, saying demand is growing in some sectors despite tariffs, with minerals and medical supported and automobiles and power transmission more exposed.

544558|2026-03.headline: Fabtech FY26 total income rose 28.4% to ₹431.33 crore, but margins compressed; management guides ~25% growth and 9.9–10.5% PAT margin.
544558|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income grew 28.4% YoY to ₹431.33 crore and EBITDA rose 18.29% to ₹55.56 crore, while reported net profit fell to ₹38.36 crore from ₹46.45 crore (FY25 included ₹17.85 crore exceptional item). Q4 total income rose 22% YoY to ₹168.24 crore and quarterly net profit rebounded to ₹22.06 crore. Margin pressure was attributed to remobilisation, a 33% rise in RMC cost and a 43% rise in execution cost, amid Middle East disruption. Cash and bank balance rose to ₹208.57 crore after a ~₹230 crore equity infusion (IPO), while receivables rose to ₹204.34 crore.

segments.name: UAE
segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue grew by about ₹126 crore (₹126.6 crore) in FY26, with two subsidiaries in Dubai.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: Revenue at about ₹82.7 crore in FY26, with a subsidiary, a JV and a local entity; vaccine and animal-health projects won.

segments.name: Kenya / Africa
segments.commentary: Kenya revenue grew by ₹43.24 crore; West and North Africa wins include a $7.05 million tablet/capsule facility in West Africa and a ~₹49–52 crore EU-GMP veterinary facility in North Africa.

segments.name: Mark Maker (33.33%)
segments.commentary: Management says this investee, a process OSD and closed-loop line division, is contributing to growth.

guidance_outlook: Management projects ~25% revenue growth (Karan Doshi cited 25–30%), with 'close to 25% or more' in closing remarks.
PAT margin targeted to improve toward 9.9%–10.5%; internal targets are contribution margin ~45%, EBITDA margin 13–14%, PAT margin 9–11%.
Order book above ₹900 crore as of March 31, 2026, to be executed over 18–24 months.

Management says it is on track for the 12–14% PAT guidance for FY28 (per Rahil's question); FY27 revenue of ₹530–600 crore from earlier conferences was not reconciled, with the difference attributed to consolidated versus standalone communication.
Q1 FY27 completion targeted for the North Africa veterinary facility.
capex_capacity: Strategic equity infusion of ~₹230 crore (IPO) to fund expansion; part earmarked for talent acquisition; the JBN acquisition in the West is under due diligence and not yet closed.
Local infrastructure in UAE and Saudi Arabia, with on-ground installation teams; in-house manufacturing covers process, air, water, containment and clean room partitions.
Stakes: 100% subsidiaries in UAE (FTS) and Saudi Arabia (Fabtech Saudi); 33.33% in Mark Maker; 16% in TSA (water systems); 49% in FABL (containment).
Pre-engineered buildings and solar integration being added to control project timelines; greenfield project timelines reduced by ~20% from 24–27 months.
Related-party procurement: ~11% of clean room panels from FTCL and ~15% of air handling units from Advantek.
demand_pricing: Order book above ₹900 crore as of March 31, 2026, including Dubai operations; split across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kenya, other Africa and North Africa (Algeria, Morocco, Egypt, Ethiopia).
Hot-lead pipeline of about $200 million with offers in the market; bid-to-win conversion stated at 11%, rising to 16–17% of hot leads.
Order sizes increasing: earlier $30–40 million, now orders up to $70 million; some orders above ₹50–60 crore.
Q4 top line about ₹150 crore; highest sales in March.

Pricing: contracts USD-denominated (LC-backed), with variation clauses for raw-material and freight cost increases. Contribution margin was 43.8% vs 45.9% prior year; RMC cost grew ~33% and execution cost ~43%.
Revenue recognised on Bill of Lading submission against LC; billing is lumpy and dependent on client civil readiness.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins shrunk despite revenue growth, and how will investor confidence be regained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project and geography mix (Africa margin pressure), remobilisation, a ~33% RMC cost increase and ~43% execution cost increase; non-contribution margin at 43.8% vs 45.9% last year. Margins expected to improve as internal margin development progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on Q4 and expected impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: No material financial impact per management; freight is the main cost pressure while RMC is sourced in India and revenue is in USD. Delivery delays are possible; no cancellations so far, and clients are discussing variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw-material and freight increases reflected in customer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts contain variation clauses, with post-detailed-engineering items priced at net present value; management says clients accept variations to avoid project delays. It is not a pass-through, but a negotiated outcome that also affects future awards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the ₹900 crore order book by geography and the timeline for conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Split across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kenya, other Africa and North Africa; to be executed over 18–24 months. Billing depends on client readiness to accept materials and complete installation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO fund deployment delayed, and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an active decision: the JBN acquisition in the West is under due diligence and talent acquisition is ongoing. Monitoring agency required ₹50 crore working-capital reimbursement to come from the monitoring account, which is now being done. Current borrowings are USD PCFC lines at about SOFR-linked rates plus 200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin target and guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal targets: contribution margin ~45%, EBITDA 13–14%, PAT 9–11%. Management said it remains on track for the 12–14% FY28 PAT guidance, with FY27 growth of about 25%.

Geopolitical exposure: Middle East war affecting logistics, visas and site access; project delays on greenfield civil works, though no cancellations reported.
Order conversion timing: booking to billing gap; 18–24 month execution of ₹900 crore order book; hot-lead conversion of 11%–17%.

Related-party dependence on FTCL (~11% of clean room panels) and Advantek (~15% of air handling units).

544558|2026-06.headline: Fabtech Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 74.98 crore and PAT turned to Rs 4.21 crore from a Rs 6.13 crore loss.
544558|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 10.3% YoY to Rs 74.98 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 7.41 crore (9% margin) versus negative Rs 5.27 crore a year ago. Contribution margin expanded about 910 bps to 46.7%, which management attributes to geography mix (Saudi Arabia, Africa) and project mix, with reduced dependence on UAE. UAE FTS faced war-related headwinds, and several large orders slipped (not cancelled) into later quarters. Management reiterated 20-25% organic growth for FY27, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 stronger, and guided PAT margin of 9-11%.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 17.14 crore, up 130% YoY. Company incorporated Specialized Contracting Activities LLC with 51% stake to pursue MEP and civil projects; one civil order already secured.

segments.name: Africa (Morocco and Kenya)
segments.commentary: Morocco and Kenya together contributed Rs 27.94 crore, both markets were not material a year ago. Botswana veterinary vaccine facility order of Rs 31.23 crore won in the quarter.

segments.name: UAE FTS
segments.commentary: Faced genuine regional headwinds from the Middle East war; no figure disclosed. Management expects UAE projects to normalise but gave no timeline.

segments.name: Standalone FTL core business
segments.commentary: Management cited a strong standalone turnaround in the core FTL business, without a disclosed figure.

segments.name: India (Fabtech Technologies Cleanrooms)
segments.commentary: Management said Fabtech Technologies Limited is international-focused; India cleanroom business sits in a separate entity. Only one India-specific contract is in the book.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 organic revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 significantly stronger.
PAT margin guidance of 9-11% with around 25% PAT growth; Aman Anavkar framed a 9.5-10% target for the year.
Proposed acquisitions in Italy (Europe) and Saudi Arabia expected to complete before FY27 year-end, subject to approvals; European deal visible in next two to three quarters.
Internal top-line ambition of Rs 1,000 crore-plus by 2030 on an organic basis; Vision 2030/2035 document in preparation.
Contracts being reworked to move toward percentage-of-completion revenue recognition; changes expected over the next few years.
capex_capacity: Up to Rs 24 crore approved as investment into Fabtech Technologies LLC (Saudi), plus additional investment into FT Institutions Private Limited.
In-house manufacturing of process air, water, utilities and process machines supports vaccine and pharma tenders.
Around Rs 400 crore of pre-engineered building (PEB) projects bid in Africa and the Middle East.
Around Rs 20-22 crore of goods lying at port at quarter end due to shipment availability constraints.
Project durations: 12-24 months after civil readiness; 12-36 months for greenfield projects.
demand_pricing: Active inquiries exceed Rs 9,300 crore; hot leads over Rs 3,800 crore. Management cited these as two-year visibility.
Several large ticket orders slipped due to geopolitical conditions and donor/government funding cycles; management said there were no cancellations but investors slowed decisions.
Repeat customers about 10% of the quarter's order intake (about Rs 8 crore); management said the company has deliberately diversified away from repeat clients.
Revenue is 78% from MENA, GCC, ECO and the Persian Gulf region per management.
Price escalation clause: pass-through of raw material cost increases above 5%; offers valid only 2-3 weeks. Management said pass-through is not always full.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables rose to about Rs 215 crore; what share is overdue and what are receivable-day expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no open credit, with receivables backed by LCs or CAD. Aging is mostly retention (10-15%, held 1-2 years), and about Rs 120 crore of Saudi receivables sit with a large customer until shipment completes, with Q3 delivery expected. Customer advances total about Rs 110 crore, and working cycle is about 120 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UAE weakness cyclical, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UAE demand is focused on high-tech facilities, cell and gene therapy labs and compounding pharmacies, with some projects delayed by geopolitics. It gave no timeline for normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Does the West Asia war affect execution and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said on-site teams kept executing, but conversions slowed as customers delayed decisions. Management said working capital has not been impacted much, and the company is using outsourced labour selectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to percentage-of-completion accounting to smooth quarterly results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is reworking contracts with auditors to define billable milestones tied to percentage completion. Existing contracts stay on shipment/milestone basis, and changes are expected over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: What progress on the IPO-proceeds acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: The Saudi acquisition (SACE, 51%) is complete. The European acquisition is in due diligence and management expects it in the next two to three quarters, with no value disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the margin expansion come from: gross margin or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both: evaluating procurement from China to lift gross margin, and fixed-cost control with operating leverage visible in Q1.

risks_watch: Revenue is H2-weighted and recognised on shipment/BL basis, so Q1 results are not a run-rate guide; Q3-Q4 must deliver to hit 20-25% growth.
Order slippage from geopolitics: Rs 900 crore+ backlog depends on conversion of delayed large orders.
Around Rs 20-22 crore of goods held at port, and Rs 120 crore Saudi receivable pending delivery in Q3.
Concentration in MENA (78% of revenue) and UAE headwinds.
Shareholder sentiment: stock below IPO price was raised repeatedly; management had no time-bound plan beyond more investor meetings and media strategy.
