544563|2026-03.headline: Zelio FY26 consolidated revenue rose 81.8% to INR313 crore, EBITDA INR38.01 crore at 12.2% margin, PAT INR28.39 crore; FY27 target 125,000 units.
544563|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) consolidated revenue from operations of INR310.71 crore (total revenue INR313.68 crore), up 81.8%, with EBITDA of INR38.01 crore and PAT of INR28.39 crore. Two-wheeler volumes reached more than 70,000 units (H1 30,000, H2 40,000+), and capacity was expanded from 72,000 to 240,000 units across four plants. Management guided to 75-80% revenue growth and more than 125,000 units in FY27, with Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) and Patan (Haryana, three-wheelers) commissioned in July 2026 per the script. The call was largely Q&A on volumes, dealers, financing, capex and governance; many answers were qualitative or repeated the same targets.

segments.name: Two-wheelers (low-speed EV scooters)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume above 70,000 units, with H2 above H1 (40,000+ vs 30,000). Average selling price cited at about INR44,000, with management expecting INR45,000-50,000 over time.

segments.name: Three-wheelers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume of only 800 units because plant was not ready. FY27 target is more than 2,000 units, with production from the Patan, Haryana plant.

segments.name: Zelio Auto Components (wholly-owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Incorporated to control component procurement and spare parts supply; management says it is already contributing positively to consolidated revenue and profitability. No separate figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of more than 125,000 units.
Revenue growth target of 75-80% YoY, described as a repeatable structural trajectory.
Dealer network to expand from more than 400 to more than 550 in FY27 (100-150 new dealers); 100% of dealerships to be exclusive by this year.
Three-wheeler FY27 target of more than 2,000 units.

Management said EBITDA and PAT margins will be maintained despite higher branding and promotion spend; marketing spend for FY27 not yet decided, with FY26 non-IPL promotional spend stated as more than INR1 crore.
Five to six vehicles to be 70-80% Make in India by 2027; components to be 100% indigenous in-house by this year or next financial year (per management).
Management said the company will move to quarterly reporting in the future, but not immediately; it is currently required to report half-yearly.
capex_capacity: Capacity expanded from 72,000 to 240,000 units per annum in FY26 across four plants.
Ladwa, Haryana flagship: 120,000 units per annum; serves North and West India.
Cuttack, Odisha: 60,000 units per annum, operational and GST-registered since December 2025; gateway to East and Northeast India.
Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu: about 60,000 units per annum, commissioned in July 2026 per the script (an answer said operational from next month); Tamil Nadu GST active.
Patan, Haryana: electric three-wheeler and two-wheeler chassis plant, commissioned in July 2026 per the script. Three-wheeler fabrication to be in-house after this plant starts.
Management said IPO proceeds funded plant and machinery, mainly for the three-wheeler segment; capital advances for new plant and machinery were about INR25 lakh.
demand_pricing: Management cited a low-speed EV segment of 8-10 lakh units per year (about 40-45% of EV two-wheeler volumes), growing 20-25% per annum, priced INR50,000-75,000 with no licence or registration needed.
Management said crude price increases and government encouragement are driving switching to EVs; expects market growth of 20-25%.
Management targets more than 10% share of the EV market this year and 20-30% within 2-3 years; an analyst's calculation implied roughly 10-11% share on 125,000 units against 11-12 lakh market.
Financing: management cited tie-ups with Bajaj, Kotak and Trusera Finance; said finance options are available in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.
Management said competition would not force price cuts; South India price list is expected to fall as Coimbatore transport costs decline.
Management said the monsoon has no effect on two-wheeler sales (IP67 motors and controllers); agricultural impact is said to delay, not reduce, sales.
Management expects 'no government support' for low-speed EVs currently beyond encouragement and registration/licence exemptions.

qa_highlights.question: Will a bad monsoon affect rural and Tier 2/3 demand, and how is consumer financing structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon does not hit sales (delays only) and cited tie-ups with Bajaj, Kotak and Trusera Finance for customer loans in Tier 1 and 2 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of INR43 crore loans and advances on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shubham Garg said supplier advances were about INR22.5 crore, capital advances INR25 lakh, and GST and customs refund claims INR19 crore, totalling about INR42.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate and how long does it last?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company has applied under Section 115BAB and pays 17% tax, which runs for 10 years from 2021, leaving about five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the Coimbatore plant produce and how does competition affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Coimbatore has about 60,000 units capacity, matching Odisha, and that lower transport costs will reduce South India prices without hurting EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin plans given higher branding spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to keep profitability and margins similar while doubling or tripling volume, and that branding spend will not dent EBITDA or PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is a bike segment planned, and how are three-wheeler service and spares handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bike plans until battery costs fall; service engineers grew from four to more than 10, and the subsidiary handles spares.

risks_watch: Management's 75-80% growth and 125,000-unit targets rely on four plants and 550+ dealers being operational; the Coimbatore and Patan commissioning dates are stated in July 2026, after the period end.
Dependence on imported components (cells, from China and elsewhere) for parts not yet indigenised; management guided 70-80% Make in India by 2027.

544563|2026-09.headline: Zelio E Mobility H1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 296.66 crore (more than double YoY), with PAT of Rs 31.39 crore and net margin above 10%.
544563|2026-09.overview: Management described H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) as the strongest half in the company's history, with consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 296.66 crore, more than double the prior-year period, and EBITDA of Rs 40.49 crore at a 13.6% margin (12% a year earlier). Profit after tax was Rs 31.39 crore, with EPS of Rs 14.24. Growth was funded partly by working capital: inventory and supplier advances pushed operating cash flow negative and borrowings up to Rs 44.82 crore, with debt-to-equity at 0.31x versus 0.18x in March. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of more than 125,000 units, 550+ dealers, and 75-80% revenue growth, and a fourth plant in Patan began commercial production on 28 October.

financial_highlights.change: margin up from 12% in H1 FY26
equal to about 98% of FY26 full-year EPS

segments.name: Two-wheeler (low speed scooters)
segments.commentary: Sold more than 62,000 units in H1 FY27 versus more than 70,000 in all of FY26. Low-speed is the bulk of sales; high-speed share is small, with 2-3 high-speed models planned next year.

segments.name: Three-wheeler (e-rickshaw / cargo, Tanga)
segments.commentary: Sold about 600 units in H1 FY27 versus about 650 in full FY26. Management targets 2,000-3,000 units from next financial year, with Patan plant intended to bring sourcing in-house.

segments.name: Export / Nepal
segments.commentary: Selling more than 160 scooters a month in Nepal; a distributor outlet opened in Kathmandu last month.

Odisha plant started production in February 2026; Coimbatore followed in July 2026.
Installed capacity is 3.12 lakh units across four plants (Haryana, Odisha, Coimbatore, Patan).

qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler volume was over 62,000 units in H1 against more than 70,000 in all of FY26; three-wheeler about 600 units against about 650 in FY26. ASP rose from about Rs 45,000 to Rs 48,000-50,000 on metal prices. Low-speed is the majority of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What are the utilisation levels of the four plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Patan 70-80%, Odisha about 50%, Coimbatore about 30%. Management expects 80% utilisation of the Patan plant within two years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market is growing about 50% a year and that the company competes on quality and service; it claims 8-9% low-speed share and targets 25% within two years.

qa_highlights.question: How will commodity inflation affect demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has not been affected by 10-15% raw material increases, as rising fuel prices have increased demand; prices have been raised across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter high-speed, and what R&D is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: High-speed entry is planned with 2-3 models next year, targeting affordable pricing. The Rs 168 crore raise funds a professional R&D team focused on motors and battery packs, and backward integration; management said results are 2-3 years away.

qa_highlights.question: Is B2B or delivery-fleet business planned, and what is the outlook for Nepal and other markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B margins and brand visibility are low, so it is focused on B2C through dealers for now, with B2B possible later when capacity is spare. Nepal sales exceed 160 scooters a month; no other international markets are active.

Other developments included a Gujarat government AI analytics order of about INR 10.97-11 crore, a TimePay prepaid card tie-up with NPST, and early Gulf (UAE) expansion. Figures were stated loosely on the call (for example "lakhs" used for crore), so the crore values should be verified against filings.

qa_highlights.question: Are further acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Nothing is in the immediate pipeline; focus is on the fish and seafood project, Meevaa and retail rollout.

risks_watch: Cash flow from operations is negative despite EBITDA; working capital needs rise with scale, and positive operating cash flow is not expected for 2-3 years.
B2C volumes flat to down and monthly active users down about 15% in H2; management attributes this to a shift of focus, so monitor B2C recovery and retention (85%).
Margin dilution from B2B-heavy mix; FY26 reported PAT includes a deferred tax impact that management says will not recur in H1 FY27.
Export and shipping exposure to the war, raw material pressures, and perishable inventory wastage risk (per management).
Meevaa targets depend on a young product; management calls the 15-20% FY27 contribution a sharp ramp, and the frozen category is competitive domestically.
544568|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, targets and the Meevaa and aquaculture strategy; more hesitant and evasive on specific numbers, such as net revenue by year, cash-flow timing and new-city capex, which were not quantified.
key_quotes: The margin profile will certainly improve, because, we are looking at 20% contribution coming in the new financial year, from the Meevaa range.
What gives us confidence today is that growth is no longer coming at the cost of profitability.
So, it's not that we are establishing it.
So, nothing is in immediate pipeline, because acquisitions takes a long time and, we have our hands full currently.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Planned new cities (Pune, Nashik, near-Bangalore) and Marina Aqua land parcels in Kanpur, Ghaziabad, Nagpur and Assam point to further investment, but no capex per city was disclosed and cash is INR 20-25 crore with negative operating cash flow.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive in 2-3 years

544569|2026-03.headline: Tata Motors Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 24,500 crore with EBITDA margin at 13.9%, but management guided only to single-digit Q1 growth amid commodity and diesel risks.
544569|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter of the year on volume and price, with wholesales of about 131.8K units (up 25% YoY) and standalone EBIT margin of 12.1%. FY26 standalone EBIT crossed 11% for the first time and free cash flow reached about Rs 9,200 crore. Management flagged a sharp commodity cost headwind (about 100 bps in Q4 and significantly higher in Q1 FY27), took only a 2% price increase in April, and said it will not pass through the full cost increase. Iveco deal closure has slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals.

segments.name: Trucks (HCV / ILMCV)
segments.commentary: Management cited highest HCV offtake market share in a decade; ILMCV (5-19 t) showed the highest growth rates through the year. 17 next-gen trucks launched at start of Q4; entire truck range now meets European cabin safety standards.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: Enters FY27 with a solid government order book; 5,000 bus orders secured from STUs during FY26. Management is focused on rebuilding share on a profitable basis; the company is not bidding aggressively on EV bus tenders, calling current quotes unsustainable.

segments.name: SCV Pickup / Small CV
segments.commentary: Ace Pro (launched June 2025) and Intra EV drove volume momentum; EV penetration in SCV pickup rose to about 7% in the last 1-2 months vs about 4% for FY26, with management expecting higher single-digit penetration.

segments.name: Parts & Services / Fleet Edge / Smart City
segments.commentary: Parts and service growth sustained at a higher trajectory; Fleet Edge subscription renewals almost doubled from Q1 to Q4. Smart City has 3,815+ cumulative e-buses deployed, ~59 crore km run, and above 96% uptime.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Largest-ever order of 70,000 Yodha and Ultra T.7 units for Indonesia secured in February; first shipment already at sea after homologation. No shipments to Middle East for the last two months; Sri Lanka under pressure from fuel availability.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 revenue growth guided at single digit, 'if not more', YoY, with management declining to give full-year visibility and pointing to quarter-by-quarter guidance.
Commodity headwind: about 100 bps impact in Q4 FY26, with significantly higher impact expected in Q1 FY27 (steel, aluminium, copper, precious metals, rupee depreciation).
A 2% price increase taken in April 2026; management does not intend to pass through the full commodity increase and will offset through cost levers.
EBITDA margin guidance is 'teens' (corrected from 'mid-teens' on the call), held quarter-by-quarter given cost headwinds.
FY27 investment spend (R&D plus capex) expected broadly in line with FY26 (Rs 3,000 crore); capex guided at 2% to 4% of revenue.

Iveco transaction closure expected in Q2 FY27; financing via bridge loan then refinancing, with the equity/debt mix still open. Final dividend of Rs 4 per share (about Rs 1,500 crore cash outflow) is subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment spend about Rs 3,000 crore: R&D about Rs 1,700 crore and capex plus other investments about Rs 1,100 crore; within the 2%-4% of revenue guidance band.
EV ramp: Intra EV in only its second month of production; management plans to ramp gradually to meet demand.
Electric trucks: 55-ton electric tractor deliveries started with BillionE Mobility; MoU with VOC port (Tamil Nadu) for 40 H2-ICE trucks trials; about 250 electric bus orders received.
Iveco acquisition pending approvals; management said most regulatory approvals are received, with only French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals outstanding.
demand_pricing: Industry TIV grew 19% YoY in Q4 FY26 while Tata Motors volumes grew 25%; FY26 TIV grew 12.5% vs company growth of 11.6%.
H1 FY26 was muted (Operation Sindoor sentiment and early monsoon); H2 recovered on GST 2.0-led consumption, with Q4 the standout quarter.
April 2026 industry volumes saw healthy double-digit growth; management says roughly half of May is in and momentum is intact.
Management claims ASPs are rising segment by segment (trucks up YoY); the blended ASP decline is attributed to higher van mix and almost no electric bus sales in FY26.
Diesel is the key monitorable: it is 30-50% of total cost of ownership for transporters; diesel sales rose 8% YoY in March but April was about flat YoY per management.
Heavy-duty customers are postponing purchases toward month-end amid diesel uncertainty; smaller vehicles see lower uncertainty.
E-way bill generation grew 15% YoY in Q4 and 12% YoY in April 2026 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook for MHCV and LCV, and how much risk do fuel price hikes pose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a single-digit Q1 growth 'if not more' and will guide quarter by quarter; diesel prices are the key monitorable as they drive 30-50% of TCO.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost pressure is expected in Q1, how much is being passed on, and what drives margins from here?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps hit in Q4 with a significantly higher impact in Q1; a 2% price increase was taken in April, with the rest absorbed through cost levers to protect demand.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 70,000-unit Indonesia order be executed, and will it finish in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Product is homologated in Indonesia and first shipment is at sea; ramp-up to be rapid, with delivery timeline to be discussed in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is causing the Iveco closure delay, and how does the activist stake affect the deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Most approvals are in; the last two financial regulatory approvals (France and Spain) are pending, pushing closure into Q2 FY27. Management is confident the investor will support the offer.

qa_highlights.question: Are ASPs falling due to discounting or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says segment ASPs are rising; the decline in blended ASP reflects higher van volumes and minimal electric bus sales versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not participating in EV bus tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Quotes in recent CESL tenders are seen as unsustainable; the company was near L2 in one sub-part of the first tender and is pursuing corporate and intercity EV bus demand instead.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 4Q working-capital inflow seasonality still hold, and what is FY27 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 working capital was managed more evenly through the year, with YTD cash flow positive after Q2; FY27 capex guided at 2%-4% of revenue.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, precious metals) and rupee depreciation, with Q1 FY27 impact expected to be significantly higher than Q4's 100 bps.
Diesel prices and their effect on transporter economics and heavy-duty purchase timing; April diesel sales were about flat YoY.
Middle East shipments halted for two months; Sri Lanka fuel shortage; geopolitical disruption to export routes.
Iveco deal: pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals, financing mix (equity vs debt) still undecided, and an activist hedge fund's stake build (6-7%).
Electric bus business: company is holding back from tenders, leaving it out of the EV bus segment for now; EV pickup penetration needs to hold near 7%.
Management has halted its quarterly transporter sentiment survey and is revisiting the methodology.

544569|2026-06.headline: Tata Motors Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 23% to ₹19,300 crore on 26% volume growth; EBITDA margin fell 60 bps to 11.7% on commodity costs.
544569|2026-06.overview: Standalone wholesales reached about 108,700 units, up 26% YoY, with growth in every product line. Revenue grew 23% to ₹19,300 crore and EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at an 11.7% margin, down 60 bps, as steel, aluminium and copper inflation was largely offset by price increases and operating leverage. Free cash flow swung to ₹1,100 crore positive from negative ₹1,800 crore, helped by a ₹3,474 crore working-capital outflow last year that did not recur and by a one-off Indonesia advance. Management guided to a double-digit Q2 domestic growth and a further 2.5% price increase from July 1, while flagging continued commodity pressure.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 domestic CV volumes expected to show healthy double-digit YoY growth, based on July trends.
Further commodity inflation (steel, rubber) expected; net price increase of 2.5% taken from July 1, 2026, with cost management as first line of defence.
Indonesia 70,000-unit order to be supplied over FY27 and FY28; ramp-up under way.

capex_capacity: Standalone capex ₹554 crore in Q1, in line with the investment plan.

Tamil Nadu demand recovering month on month and close to normal in June.
Tipper utilisation seasonally lower during monsoon, expected to pick up mid-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic CV growth be double digit for full year, and how do Indonesia dispatches split across FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early for full-year view; Q2 expected to show double-digit growth. Indonesia 70,000 units to be supplied over FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV demand outlook, Intra EV response and capacity, and will the Q2 price hike cover cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: EV demand seen as positive, with over 850 e-bus orders and further PM e-Bus Sewa tenders expected. Capacity is not the constraint; imported cell lead times are. Further commodity pressure expected; 2.5% net price hike from July 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a limit to price hikes given steel and rubber surges, and how is discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost containment is the first lever; price increases are needed beyond that. The MY26 range helped stabilise prices. Cumulative price increase this year described as significant; no discounting figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital and FCF strength structural or one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly carry-over from Q4 and working-capital discipline plus operating profit. The Indonesia advance was a one-off that helped Q1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: E-truck profitability versus ICE and PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Profitability currently lower than ICE trucks because of low scale; will improve with scale and localisation. Some EV trucks delivered before PLI certificates due to regulatory delays, to meet customer commitments.

qa_highlights.question: How are operators' profitability and freight rates faring after diesel price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no index; anecdotally, diesel increases are being passed through and operator profitability should recover gradually.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, rubber) and further cost pressure in Q2 against a 2.5% July price hike.
Supply constraints in castings, forgings and sheet metal, and imported EV cell lead times, which could cap volumes.
Cash tax now recurring (₹500 crore in Q1 vs ₹20 crore a year earlier); Q1 working-capital benefit partly one-off from Indonesia advance.
Regulatory delay in PLI certificates for EV trucks, with some vehicles delivered before PLI approval.
Iveco transaction approval timing (one approval pending) and tender offer schedule.
Fleet utilisation still below prior-year Q1 levels; tipper utilisation seasonality.

544569|2026-09.overview: Wholesales grew 42% YoY to 135,100 units, with every segment in double digits and international business up 177% on the Indonesia order. Standalone EBITDA was about ₹2,800 crore (up 31%) and EBIT margin was 9.7%, down 50 bps YoY, as commodity inflation was largely offset by operating leverage, cost efficiency and realisation gains. Free cash flow reached ₹4,600 crore, helped by a ₹2,679 crore working capital release that management said is partly timing-related. Management expects Q3 YoY growth to taper to high single or early double digits, and commodity inflation of a further 150-200 bps in Q3.

Commodity headwind of 590 bps in Q2 EBIT margin walk; steel at a 52-week high, up about 40% YoY. Management has requested a review of the steel safeguard duty through SIAM and other channels.
Interest rates: a 25 bps hike has been taken. Management flagged diesel prices and interest rates as key demand monitorables.
No credit stress seen among transport financiers the company has spoken to. Management says they are in a good place, though not all financiers were engaged.

544570|2026-09.headline: WeWork India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to INR768.7 crore and EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, with PAT up 67.4% to INR65.8 crore.
544570|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: revenue grew 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ to about INR768.7 crore, and EBITDA rose 37.6% YoY to INR162.9 crore at a 21.2% margin. The company added a record ~11,700 desks in the quarter, taking capacity to 145,300 desks across 85 centres, while occupancy rose 357 bps YoY to 83.7%. Net debt of INR310 crore a year ago turned into net cash of INR23 crore, and ROCE reached 34.5%. Management guided to 150,000-155,000 desks by March 2027, and the company is laying out a 190,000-200,000 seat path. All figures are on an IGAAP-equivalent basis.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: VAS revenue INR79.6 crore, up 35% YoY; management says VAS is margin accretive. Customization revenue about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR29.2 crore, up 46% YoY, operating at close to 80% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Desk count expected at about 150,000-155,000 by March 2027 (145,300 at Sept 30; ~4,500 added by Oct 5, so already ~150,000); some March deliveries could slip to early April.

FY27 capex about INR500-odd crore for the full year (H2 lower than H1's INR363.8 crore, though one large deal adds capex). FY28 capex likely near INR600 crore or slightly more.
FCFO-to-EBITDA conversion expected in a 1.2x-1.5x range.

Bengaluru 54,000 desks (anchor); Hyderabad 20,000 (now second-largest, overtook Mumbai); Pune 17,000.

demand_pricing: Revenue-to-rent multiple at an all-time high of 2.7x; new large managed-office deals are at about 3x, driven by higher capex per sq ft.

Locked-in core revenue grew ~66% to INR3,843 crore against INR1,421 crore of rent, about 2.7x coverage (management also cites ~2.9x in Q&A).
Enterprises 77% of core revenue; GCCs ~41% of mix; other global companies ~26%; Fortune 500 ~30%; top 10 members 23% of revenue.
Minimum wage increases in Karnataka near 60% and backdated BESCOM energy tariffs pressured opex per sq ft in H1; management says margin would be ~22%-23% without these.

qa_highlights.question: How has underwriting changed for new centres (payback, revenue-to-rent) given rising competition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is taking larger positions in Grade A assets, underwriting buildings under development, and doing multi-property deals; it says underwriting is smarter but not drastically changed versus two years ago. Payback periods are improving and capex control is driving better returns.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal trends and pricing on renewals versus new contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal rate 80%-85% in H1; renewal escalations are lower than contracted escalations and pricing on fill-up, as management trades price for loyalty and scale. Around 50% of customer growth comes from existing members expanding.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation between expansion and FCF, and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: More FY28 expansion is planned with additional capex; the company is also looking at buybacks or dividends once book losses are cleared, and at investing in adjacent businesses that help Indian companies scale.

qa_highlights.question: Customization revenue in Q2 and EBITDA flow-through; GCC hiring outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization was about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA; management says large lumpiness is normalised. Management sees GCCs continuing to set up in India and expects demand to grow, with premium managed offices and more amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Will March 2027 desk target of 155,000 be met, and what H2 margin uplift to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Already at about 150,000 desks; 155,000 visibility by March, though some deliveries may slip into early April. Margins to expand further in Q3 and Q4, with the larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire. Q4 YoY margin change expected to be modest given a strong Q4 last year.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for next year and pipeline beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise percentage guidance; FY28 EBITDA margin range of 20%-23%, depending on capacity timing. Pipeline: about 2 million sq ft of additional prospective space not yet signed; leases signed about 12 months out with ~95% visibility, 70%-80% at 18-24 months.

544572|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
544572|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

Other expenses rose on royalty and trademark payments (about INR 60 million higher) and manufacturing costs (repairs, power and fuel, stores). A transfer pricing margin on services from SKF India was also booked.
Competition described as intense, especially at OEMs. Rupee depreciation is a bigger cost headwind than steel and oil-linked inflation.

qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags are extra investments in Pune including the new plant, intense OEM competition, higher railway mix, and higher depreciation. Management targets around 15% through 2030 and says 16-18% is an aspiration that cannot yet be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30. New Pune plant expected to be operational mid-2028, with full ramp-up and channel transfers complete by end of 2028.

qa_highlights.answer: The investment is plant and machinery for DGBB and TRB channels at the new Pune plant, not warehouses. Growth is guided at about 8% in the interim, supported by job-work from SKF India and sourcing from Ahmedabad and Nilai.

544576|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR80.54 bn (+8.1% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell ~250 bps YoY to 11.7%, with FY27 targeting early double-digit margins.
544576|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was LG Electronics India's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR80.54 bn, up 8.1% YoY, with EBITDA of INR9.45 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of INR6.93 bn (8.5%). Year-on-year margin compression was attributed to channel promotion spend (~1.1 pp), rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY, ~1 pp impact), and e-waste compliance cost (~0.2 pp). For FY26, revenue grew 1.0% to INR246.05 bn, EBITDA was INR24.08 bn (9.8%) and PAT INR16.85 bn (6.8%). Management guided FY27 to mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margins, citing April-May sell-through and recent price hikes.

qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said the new categories serve both: chest freezers (five models, market ~INR3,000 crore), fixed-speed RACs, and large refrigerators from Pune, which target new domestic business and global markets.

544584|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 50% to Rs 318 crore; EBITDA margin 10% and PAT margin 6%, with polymer flame-retardant capacity not yet commercial.
544584|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 318 crore, up about 50% from Rs 212 crore in FY25, with EBITDA margin up from 9% to 10% and PAT margin up from 5% to 6%. Sales volume rose from about 32,000-33,000 MT to 46,000 MT, which management said includes about 4,400 MT from in-house manufacturing. Management attributed H2 growth to raw-material price increases from January, volume sales, and sourcing ahead of demand, and said H2 gross margin was squeezed by those input costs. The halogen-free polymer flame-retardant plant (400 MT/month) is still in teething trouble and is expected to be commercial in the next three to six months. Many answers were forward-looking or deferred, and the call was largely Q&A from individual investors.

544587|2026-03.headline: Midwest Ltd FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3% to INR645 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin 27.0% and PAT margin 16.5%, with Quartz start-up weighing on profitability.
544587|2026-03.overview: Midwest reported FY26 consolidated revenue of INR645 crores, up about 3% from INR626 crores, with consolidated EBITDA margin of 27.01% (vs 27.43%) and PAT margin of 16.49% (vs 17.17%). Q4 revenue was INR215 crores, with EBITDA margin of 27% (vs 23.7% in Q3) and PAT margin of 17.16% (vs 13.48%). Granite standalone held margins at 27.55% EBITDA and 17.47% PAT, while the new Quartz segment absorbed about INR6 crores of cost in the year. Management said Quartz began full production in April 2026 and targets about 60% utilisation of its 300,000 tonne installed capacity in FY27, with Phase 2 commissioning expected in Q4 FY27. Debt fell by INR50 crores and working capital days fell from 122 to 104.

segments.name: Granite
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin 27.55% and PAT margin 17.47% in FY26, marginally up year on year. Management guides 10-12% organic growth; a Q4 logistics disruption from the war left about 3,000+ CBM unshipped, worth about INR25 crores of revenue.

segments.name: Quartz (processing)
segments.commentary: New segment; full production began in April 2026 after initial technical issues, with about 2,000 tonnes in the first month and targets of about 5,000 tonnes and 10,000 tonnes in the following months. Q4 sales were about 1,000+ tonnes, turnover about INR1.8 crores, and it drove about INR6 crores of cost in the consolidated numbers.

segments.name: Diamond wire
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR25 crores vs about INR16 crores in the comparative period, with PBT margin about 15%.

Quartz targets at least 60% utilisation of the 300,000 tonne Phase 1 capacity in FY27, with quarter-on-quarter growth; margins expected to improve beyond about 70% utilisation.

Price increase of about 4% negotiated with export buyers for the coming year to offset a 4-5% cost impact from fuel.

capex_capacity: Quartz Phase 1: installed capacity 300,000 tonnes, with 80% (240,000-250,000 tonnes) treated as the practical peak; split about 70% engineered stone and 30% solar glass (solar priced about INR7,000/tonne; engineered stone INR9,000-14,500 ex-plant).

Quartz Phase 2: build started April 2026, capex INR125-130 crores, commissioning targeted Q4 FY27, with the first products engineered stone and solar, and HPQ following about a quarter after commissioning.
HPQ (high-purity quartz): about 20,000 tonne plant planned; the target is to be operational in about nine months.
Rare earths: a pilot plant with KMML (six months, about INR20 crores budget, mobile unit), starting around early July 2026, followed by a commercial plant in about 8 months and about a year to build.

Sri Lanka heavy mineral sands: exploration licence being converted to a mining licence after the government's new policy (expected June 2026); plant construction planned to begin around August, taking 9-12 months.
Captive solar: about 1 MW operating; a further 0.6 MW to be ordered; renewables about 10% of energy need, with the goal of replacing fossil fuel on trucks with EVs.
demand_pricing: Granite demand strong in domestic and Chinese markets; exports of blocks to Middle East, Algeria and Egypt added as new markets, with those buyers switching from slabs to blocks.
Quartz (solar) realisation about INR7,000/tonne ex-plant; engineered stone realisation INR9,000-14,500/tonne across four grades.
Off-take for HPQ expected to be mainly China (crucible makers) initially, with India about 2-3 years away; management says it has cut out about 5-6 months from the supply chain.
Energy costs about 17-18% of total cost, now about 12-13% fossil-based; fuel price increases are causing 4-5% cost pressure.

qa_highlights.answer: Granite standalone is intact (EBITDA 27.55%, PAT 17.47%). Quartz start-up costs and fixed costs of about INR6 crores reduced PAT to INR106 crores from INR112 crores, and margins should stabilise as utilisation rises.

qa_highlights.answer: Target at least 60% of 300,000 tonne capacity (about 150,000 tonnes); peak achievable 75-80%; margins to improve beyond about 70% utilisation.

qa_highlights.answer: Study in progress; by next quarter management expects clarity. Management sees oxides as the bigger gap (PLI demand about 2,500-3,000 tonnes vs IREL about 400 tonnes) and a magnet plant costs about INR1,000-1,300 crores.

544597|2026-09.headline: Piramal Finance Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 67% YoY to INR545 crores; Growth AUM up 30% YoY and RoAUM 2% annualised.

Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

544600|2026-03.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.

India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?

No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion focus on saturating existing pincodes or entering new ones, and what about cannibalisation?

qa_highlights.question: Is same-day delivery a near-term target and does the store network become an inventory model?

segments.name: AMC (SSG partnership)
segments.commentary: Pending regulatory approvals. Management said AMC hiring will add cost, and AMC revenue was not disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Commodities and bonds
segments.commentary: Commodities launched a little over a year ago; commodity ADTO market share will be disclosed after the one-year mark. Bonds secondary market launched after primary.

guidance_outlook: Cost to operate (Groww platform) rises in Q1 FY27 due to a one-time appraisal increase, then stays broadly flat in absolute terms for the rest of the year, excluding risk-related costs.
Cost to serve expected to fall as a share of revenue, though absolute tech and AI costs rise.
Cost to grow expected to rise slightly from INR 450-500 crore but grow more slowly than revenue. Q1 marketing spend is seasonally higher (IPL), and FY27 spend is expected to be slightly above FY26.
Margin expansion depends on revenue growth: management said margins expand above about 15% revenue growth and more so at about 30%; they do not expand at lower growth.
Management expects FY27 to be the inflection point for AI in customer experience and productivity. No algo or API strategy yet, pending regulatory clarity.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose QoQ, mainly due to the Fisdom acquisition.
Employee cost rose QoQ on investment in AMC, wealth and AI, with headcount at about 1,800.

demand_pricing: Industry growth: management cited about 10-15% CAGR over the long run, with step-ups in bull markets. It said the industry is still away from the bottom, with FIIs negative and tariffs weighing on sentiment.
Acquisition funnel has shifted toward mutual funds and ETFs since September 2024. SIPs remain a major source of AUM accumulation.
Customer AUM dipped on an M2M basis in March 2026, but inflows held up as most customers stayed in profit after 31 March. Management said April was better than March.
Stock advisory and MF advisory demand is among the highest voice-of-customer requests; launch timing not set.
Settlement: customers choose bill-to-bill, monthly or quarterly settlement; quarterly is the default most customers prefer.

qa_highlights.question: How have customer cohorts from 2023-24 performed through the market correction, and how does their behaviour differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition has shifted toward MF and ETF; SIP flows continue. Most customers are still profitable, and the March dip was mainly M2M. No cohort-level AUM data was given.

qa_highlights.question: Equity F&O market share jumped to 10.6% from 9.1%. What drove it, and what is the algo share?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were new customers, initiatives including 915, and higher quarterly transacting customers (about 17 lakh vs 14 lakh). Algo and API volumes are not meaningful, and there is no algo strategy yet.

qa_highlights.question: Did employee cost and depreciation rise because of Fisdom, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose mainly due to Fisdom. Employee cost rose on investment in AMC, wealth and AI. Headcount is about 1,800.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF customer profile and what is the average MTF book?
qa_highlights.answer: No study was done. MTF is mostly used by existing customers, not as an acquisition product. The average book will be disclosed later, and the peak was around end-January or February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and the cost to acquire customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion depends on revenue growth, with about 15% as a threshold. Cost to grow is largely acquisition spend, is roughly fixed on an annual basis, and Q1 is seasonally higher.

qa_highlights.question: Industry active clients have plateaued near 50 million. What supports growth, and are there open interest limits or settlement changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth depends on bull markets; long-run industry CAGR is about 10-15%. Open interest is under half the limit on average and was not hit in Q4. Quarterly settlement is customer choice, not a regulatory mandate.

Regulatory risk on F&O and speculation curbs; management said it engages regulators at industry level.
Fisdom and wealth investment needs and FY28 profitability target; wealth scale-up is still early.
Pending SSG AMC approvals and AMC integration costs.

544603|2026-06.headline: Groww Q1 FY27 call: management gave few hard numbers; MTF yield fixed at 14.95%, cash yields up ~5% YoY, and F&O softness attributed to volatility, not SEBI rules.
544603|2026-06.overview: Management, led by co-founders Lalit Keshre (CEO) and Ishan Bansal (CFO), framed the quarter around building a wealth management platform and launching multiple products. Credit (LAS) now makes up 34% of disbursements, bonds launched last quarter are scaling, and SEBI and CCI approvals were received for the State Street Global partnership in the AMC. Management attributed F&O and order softness to volatility and to gold/silver ETF slowdown rather than regulation, and said Q4 FY26 was an anomaly for MTF and derivatives. Several data requests were declined or deferred, including CAC detail, revenue split, Fisdom/AMC revenue, and new-customer ARPU.

segments.commentary: MTF growth ahead of plan partly on markets; ticket size rising, but early Q2 MTF book flattish per analyst, which management tied to end-of-quarter market moves. LAS is 34% of disbursements.

segments.name: Broking (cash and F&O)
segments.commentary: Management says F&O dip in June-July tracked volatility (Iran war news), not SEBI rules. Cash order decline is mainly ETF (gold/silver) slowdown, per management. Derivatives are stabilising vs Q3.

segments.commentary: More than 28% retail share of notional ADTO; described as at an advanced adoption stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost rise a sign of hiring for a wealth transition, and what is the 2-3 year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said the rise is mainly the April appraisal cycle, not headcount. Headcount is not expected to rise significantly, with wealth to be AI- and tech-led alongside RMs. ESOPs are about 10% of employee cost in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is MTF yield accretive for the cash business, and how far can acceptance go?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash yields are up ~5% YoY and are expected to rise 1-2 pp per quarter as MTF penetration grows. Adoption is still early, and ticket size can expand as infra issues are resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did active derivatives customers soften sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said Q4 FY26 was an exception with war-driven volatility that started in Q4. Compared with Q3, the trend is improving and stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and scope of US stock options via GIFT City, and effect of F&O margin changes?
qa_highlights.answer: US stocks licensed and in testing, launch 'soon' with no exact date; start with US stocks. On the expiry margin news, management said it cannot comment on news, and the Nov 2024 change cannot be isolated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the July F&O dip due to SEBI rules, and is the cash order decline 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the F&O dip to volatility (Iran war news), with regulation impact smaller than the industry expected and not material for Groww. The cash order decline reflects slowing ETF (gold/silver) activity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CAC rise sharply, and what is the affluent customer retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said the rise reflects about two months of IPL spend versus one week in Q4, with brand benefit and weaker acquisition. Affluent retention is near 100% because AUM stickiness is high.

544603|2026-09.headline: Groww's Q2 FY27 call centred on Cost to Serve rising on AI compute, one-time INR10-13 crore hit, and MTF book adding ~INR600-700 crore a quarter.
544603|2026-09.overview: Management explained that Cost to Serve rose in Q2 due to AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed files on an expiry day. Cost to Grow fell because the IPL branding spend in Q1 did not recur. Management said the margin trading facility (MTF) book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter on average, with volatility from stock-level moves and policy changes such as higher haircuts on crowded stocks. Other operating income rose on about 30 IPOs (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. Management said the call was qualitative on several items, such as US stocks timing and UPI MDR outcome, and gave few new numbers on AUM or market share.

segments.name: Broking (cash and derivatives)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue in derivatives and commodities is driven by order count at INR20 per order, while cash revenue depends on both order size and count (lower of 10 bps or INR20). Cash market share has been about 15% and derivatives about 11% over the last three to four quarters, per analyst. August was the lowest volume month of Q2.

segments.name: Wealth (Groww Prime, MF Prime, Fisdom)
segments.commentary: Wealth AUM was disclosed for the first time; management said MF Prime is small. Users rose by almost 50% quarter-on-quarter, mainly from Groww Prime per analyst. Wealth income is reported within other operating income, and Fisdom users are now included in active customers.

segments.name: Lending (MTF, personal loans, loan against shares)
segments.commentary: MTF book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter. Loan against shares was launched in the last two quarters with good early traction; personal loan book is growing gradually quarter-on-quarter. No figures were given for the lending book size.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.commentary: Rose sequentially on about 30 IPOs in the quarter (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. IPO and BSDA income were regrouped out of stocks revenue.

guidance_outlook: Cost to Grow for FY27 is expected to stay in the INR400-500 crore a year range, with more spend in good markets and less in weak ones.
Management expects the MTF book to keep growing, adding about INR600-700 crore a quarter, and MTF share of cash turnover to rise over time.
Management expects the CAS rule change to normalise volumes, with faster recovery depending on the effective date, which was awaited.
Management expects UPI MDR outcome to be not materially cost-changing, but the cap level (INR300 mentioned) is still under discussion with the regulator.
Management expects long-term convergence of cash and F&O market share toward NSE active share, but said this could take around 10 years.
capex_capacity: Management said 915 power-trading tools and web-based trading are not yet a material contributor to volume or revenue.
AI spend is rising: in-house AI stack being built to lower per-token cost; AI-related costs and compute costs rose in Q2.
Compute cost scales with trading days; management uses more compute on trading days and much less on non-trading days.
Company said the wealth integration (Fisdom) is complete and some products are being mainstreamed across apps.
demand_pricing: Management said competitive pricing approach is to give customers more value than they are charged, and it is not following competitors on price.
Analyst noted some discount brokers cut brokerage by half; management did not directly address this.
Volumes were affected by the CAS circular; management expects CAS changes to normalise volumes, with derivatives largely unaffected by the proposed options.
Customers using more than two products exceed 50%; over 5% use more than four products.
US stocks product is in early beta testing with good customer feedback; no timeline for full launch was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Cost to Grow fall sharply while Cost to Serve rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to Grow fell because the Q1 IPL branding cost did not recur. Cost to Serve rose on AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed expiry-day files.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off MTF cost in September, as in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off cost as such, though MTF costs were present. Policy changes now include higher haircuts (up to 80% on some crowded stocks) and more frequent approved-list reviews, including industry-level book checks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order per ADTV rising while broking revenue is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Derivatives and commodity revenue is per order, not per ADTV, and cash revenue depends on the asset mix (ETFs vs small caps). Ticket size shifts drive the difference, and cash brokerage per order is about INR15-16 versus INR20 in F&O.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NSE active market share not reflected in cash and F&O market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects convergence over the long term as customers age and trade more and MTF grows, but noted it will not be quarter-to-quarter and may take about 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UPI MDR impact on cost to serve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still awaiting the final outcome. It expects no material cost change, but the cap (INR300 discussed) is critical and the company will push to lower it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost to grow run-rate for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around INR125 crore is the current average; H2 spend will depend on market conditions, with more spend if markets do well and less in weak markets.

544606|2026-03.headline: Pine Labs FY26 revenue grew about 19% with adjusted EBITDA up to Rs.559 Crores in Q4; FY27 revenue guided to 21%-23.5%.
544606|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as delivering about 19% full-year revenue growth, roughly 500 bps EBITDA margin expansion, and full-year PAT of about Rs.113 Crores. Q4 operating cash flow was about Rs.676 Crores, but management said this should not be viewed in isolation, with full-year operating cash flow at about Rs.395 Crores. Q4 growth shortfall was attributed mainly to infrastructure deployment delays (about 2 lakh POS machines backlogged due to a chip shortage) and softness in Middle East and airline business. The company gave a hard FY27 revenue growth guidance of 21%-23.5%, and said Q1 FY27 would be at the lower end.

financial_highlights.change: H2 FY26 growth about 20%-21% per management
vs Rs.357 Crores in the year-ago quarter
About 50% growth per analyst question, not disputed
Run-rate capex about Rs.180-190 Crores after adjusting for older DCP payments

segments.name: Digital infrastructure and transactions
segments.commentary: Covers offline infrastructure (about 2 million touchpoints), flow/transaction services, and fintech infrastructure for banks and merchants. Management expects at least 2%-3% improvement in infrastructure growth versus earlier assumptions.

segments.name: Issuing and acquiring
segments.commentary: Now about 30% of revenue. Issuing growing in India and globally; employee benefits program to launch in the next few weeks to quarters; stablecoin-backed prepaid platform sales to start within a month.

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Online business grew about 60% YoY; all three large e-commerce and top three quick-commerce players use Pine Labs as a platform. Shopflo acquisition is product-led and not material to growth; guidance excludes inorganic contribution.

segments.name: International (IAP)
segments.commentary: International growing about 44% per management; Philippines has five clients including GCash; POS services launched in Singapore; two head-to-head wins against global payment majors.

Q1 FY27 expected at the lower end of the range; growth to improve in Q2, Q3 and Q4.
Management did not give specific EBITDA guidance for FY27 but expects significant adjusted EBITDA improvement; reiterated 55% incremental contribution-to-EBITDA conversion as a floor.

Operating cash flow expected to improve significantly in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 tracking to the 21%-23% guidance and will growth be consistent across quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident in the hard guidance; Q4 shortfall was about Rs.20-25 Crores from infrastructure deployment delays and Middle East softness. Q1 expected at the lower end of the range, improving from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Affordability take rate fell from about 35 bps to 30 bps and working capital cycle shortened; is this the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30 bps is a blended flow take rate affected by UPI and DCC mix; pure affordability take rates remain strong. Working capital held at 14%-15% beyond early settlement; bill discounting is an ongoing program, not one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Is there headroom to monetize GTV growth of about 50% when revenue grew 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; monetization varies by segment (transaction- or value-based). Value-based revenue and data services are growing and recurring revenue is most of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: How many net new terminals will the OMC contract add and what additional services does it bring?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50,000 of 130,000 terminals deployed; OMC revenue includes forecourt integration, loyalty and IOT tenders. Indian Oil extra power loyalty contract is about Rs.60-65 Crores over five years, worth about 30-40 bps of growth uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split between affordability and VAS, and what drove the CM question?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split affordability and VAS. Contribution margin is net-revenue based (distribution is the only gross line); a 2%-3% variance is expected from mix as employee benefits launch.

risks_watch: Chip and component supply delays on POS deployment; Q1 FY27 deliveries and CWIP conversion.
Working capital and early-settlement reliance (Rs.202 Crores inflows in Q4) and whether take rates hold near 30 bps.

Geopolitical effects on Middle East and airline revenue and cross-border flows.

544606|2026-06.headline: Pine Labs Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 20% YoY, but adjusted EBITDA of Rs.126 Crores fell short of the ~Rs.135-140 Crores management said it would have liked, due to front-loaded investments.
544606|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 revenue grew about 20% YoY, at the lower end of the 21-23.5% full-year guidance, which it described as expected for Q1. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about Rs.126 Crores, below the level management said it wanted, after front-loaded spend on cloud, network and sales headcount (about 500 salespeople added over six months). PAT was close to Rs.20 Crores on PBT of about Rs.38 Crores, with an effective tax rate of about 46% due to losses in international entities that are not tax-recognised. Operating cash flow/working capital was about 16% of revenue against guidance to stay under 15% for the full year. DITP India growth was 20-25%, while the reported 4% DITP GTV growth was driven by bill payments with one client moving transactions in-house.

Management said it would have liked about Rs.135-140 Crores

Credit processing business about Rs.100 Crores annualised revenue, present in about 20 countries.

segments.commentary: Online and bill payments historically growing about 50%+; new online clients added include IRCTC, Zepto, Croma, Reliance Digital and Lenskart.com.

qa_highlights.question: Why did issuing and acquiring contribution margin dip and will distribution growth keep pressuring margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution-led market entry (e.g., Singapore, US restaurant chain) carries lower margins; contribution margin should be 73-74% for full year with H2 higher from festive processing and flow mix. Lower-margin low-margin device sales (25-30% of deployments) also weighed on margin.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin dip and is the cost recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cloud costs rose about Rs.10-12 Crores QoQ (25-30% expected to recur) and network costs about Rs.10 Crores (about 50% expected to recur). Management would have liked about Rs.135-140 Crores adjusted EBITDA versus Rs.126 Crores reported.

qa_highlights.question: Will OMC contracts contribute fully and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of the full-term contract value has been captured; the rest expected in Q2 and Q3. Rollouts of 90,000-100,000 terminals are underway.

qa_highlights.question: What is India DITP GTV growth excluding bill payments?
qa_highlights.answer: India DITP growth around 20-25%; the 4% GTV growth was largely due to bill payments volume moved in-house by one client.

qa_highlights.question: Why did absolute contribution margin not grow more and are there investments above the line?
qa_highlights.answer: No marketing investment above contribution; sub-contribution costs (distribution listing fees, network) and below-line investments were described; management said EBITDA margin in distribution business is expanding year on year.

qa_highlights.question: How big is international losses and when will they break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose per-subsidiary losses. Mature markets like Malaysia are profitable; Singapore and Dubai expected to break even in one to two years. Q1 PBT about Rs.38 Crores, ETR 46%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the issuing/distribution model tie up working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Pine Labs does not pre-purchase inventory or lend against brand inventory; card inventory is created at point of sale. Working capital about 16% in Q1 due to Q1 payouts, with full-year 13-15% guidance reaffirmed.

544606|2026-09.headline: Pine Labs Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 24% YoY and adjusted EBITDA about 27%; management now expects FY27 revenue growth above 23-23.5%.
544606|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as strong execution, with revenue up about 24% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up about 27%. Management said each business line (offline, issuing, online) grew faster than the market and gained share. Flow-based income rose about 25% YoY while UPI volumes grew about 50%. Management plans to add about 10 lakh soundboxes and sales headcount, and said H2 EBITDA should be well above H1 and FY EBITDA margin should be at least 21%. Analysts pressed on EBITDA margin dilution, UPI MDR economics, capex and indirect cost step-ups; management answered most with qualitative explanations and few new numbers.

segments.name: Enterprise offline
segments.commentary: Management said it retained 100% of enterprise accounts with strong net revenue retention and added Tanishq across all stores in Q2.

segments.name: Mid-market offline
segments.commentary: Nearly 100,000 terminals deployed on a trailing 12-month basis; mid-market cohorts (apparel, F&B, duty free, airports) cited as growing about 39-40%.

segments.name: Issuing (prepaid and gift cards)
segments.commentary: Processing share about 80-85%; distribution grew faster than market. NCMC distribution about 1,000 cards per day, Bharat Yatra 25,000-30,000 cards per month; employee tax benefit card due end November/early December.

segments.name: Online and bill payments
segments.commentary: Top four Q-commerce companies use the gateway; one of the largest consumer billers signed up, going live in Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE about 1 lakh transactions per day (Emirates NBD, Wio Bank); close to 1 lakh POS in Malaysia; 50,000 POS in Philippines; present in about 22 countries. Singapore gift card distribution reduced in Q2 after a large retailer exited, with EBITDA impact called immaterial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected above the 23-23.5% guided at start of year, per CEO closing remarks.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin expected at least 21% (CEO said 'at least 21'), versus 18% in H1 as described by analyst.
H2 EBITDA expected to be much higher than H1; EBITDA expected to keep expanding over time as flow-based income grows.
Working capital guided at 13-15% of top line for full year; Q3 seasonally weaker cash flow expected.
Contribution margin guided at 72-75% overall, with issuing 52-55% and DITP 81-83%.
Effective tax rate declined vs prior quarter; management gave medium to long-term tax guidance (no figures stated).
capex_capacity: About 10 lakh (1 million) additional soundboxes planned to capture UPI transactions at existing merchants; management said soundboxes cost about Rs.500-600 and capex impact is immaterial.
H1 capex about Rs.240 Crore, including about Rs.35 Crore slipped from Q4 FY26 and about Rs.20-25 Crore of advances (vendors now asking about 80% advance versus 20% earlier) due to chip shortages.
Full-service POS deployments continue at natural pace; not part of the 10 lakh soundbox plan.
Capex described as normalising; management expects steady state across the two years after adjusting for these items.
demand_pricing: UPI accounts for about 75-77% of POS transactions; those transactions grew about 68% compounded over last two years; management expects about 70% growth next year.

UPI MDR: 40 bps cited as the headline rate, with about 11 bps retained by acquirer; implementation timing with NPCI, which management said it does not control. Analyst's sensitivity of Rs.80-230 Crore range (from 5-6 bps to full 40 bps on about Rs.4 lakh Crore run-rate) was described as directionally correct, but management said it books income only when received.
Management said no pricing pressure in offline or online; online price increases by peers allowed Pine Labs to gain share.
Management said soundbox pricing will be transaction-based rather than a Rs.125-130 rental, as merchants will not pay both.
Affordability (EMI) growth now broader than CDIT, with non-CDIT volumes rising; October Navratri and Dussehra described as strong, Diwali read pending over about two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will India issuing and acquiring growth (about 40%) accelerate in Q3 given festive season timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Navratri and Dussehra were strong and Diwali visibility comes in about two weeks; growth drivers cited were new use cases such as refund wallets and gaming, not seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Does the UPI GTV outlook for FY28 (about 60% growth) rest on the device count plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied it to UPI shift on POS (75-77% of transactions) and to 10 lakh additional soundboxes to capture missed UPI volumes at existing merchants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable GMV and take rate under the UPI MDR change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to estimate net take rate, citing commercial negotiations and possible MCC-based pricing; said only volumes were provided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international revenue mix dip and does it affect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to a large global retailer's exit from Singapore gift card distribution, a low-margin business; EBITDA impact called immaterial and revenue for Q2 already reflected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin tracking below last year and will guidance be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales hiring pays back over about nine months, and it does not plan to cut EBITDA guidance; expects at least 21% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex and indirect costs rise in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex overflow from Q4 (about Rs.35 Crore) and Rs.20-25 Crore advances; indirect cost includes cloud and data at 8.5-9% of top line, outsourced field staff, and GFF sponsorship which fell in Q2 this year versus Q3 last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash flow and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 cash flow strong but not to be extrapolated; FY net working capital expected in 13-15% of top line, with Q3 seasonally weaker.

risks_watch: UPI MDR implementation timing and net take rate remain in NPCI's hands; management has not included it in guidance.
Diwali affordability and EMI performance, with electronics price inflation affecting GMV.
Sales-led investment (headcount, international, soundboxes) pressuring margins for about nine months before productivity.
Chip shortage causing capex slippage and higher vendor advances.
Issuing GTV volatility from brand promotion cyclicality; management said GTV understates revenue impact.

544608|2026-03.headline: Emmvee FY26 revenue rose 116% to INR 5,049 crore and PAT 193% to INR 1,082 crore, with 9.4 GW order book and 6 GW expansion underway.
544608|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year as a listed company (IPO Nov 2025, INR 2,900 crore raised), with revenue of INR 5,049 crore, EBITDA of INR 1,734 crore (34% margin) and PAT of INR 1,082 crore (21% margin). Module capacity reached 10.3 GW after two 2.5 GW lines were commissioned (May and Dec 2025), and cell utilisation rose to 69.9% for the year and 79% in Q4. Working capital absorbed cash as inventory built up, while the 6 GW integrated cell and module project at Devanahalli is progressing with IREDA's INR 3,306 crore loan sanctioned. Management stated that FY27 will be a year of execution.

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 10.3 GW at March 31, 2026, 100% TOPCon; module utilisation 43% for FY26, affected by Units 5 and 6 running only part-year. Q4 module production about 953 MW per management in Q&A, and G12R modules now in production.

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 2.94 GW; utilisation 69.9% in FY26 (43.3% in FY25), 79% in Q4 and about 85% in March 2026. Management expects a transition from M10 to G12R cells by end of the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: 6 GW integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli: module line commissioning expected by end of calendar 2026, cell line by end of FY27.
Post-expansion installed capacity targeted at 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end of FY27.
Ingot and wafer facility of about 9 GW in phases: Phase 1 5 GW, Phase 2 4 GW a year later; first facility planned in FY29. Capex guided at INR 600-700 crore per GW.
Next-quarter DCR mix guided at 30-35% of module sales; by around the beginning of FY28 management expects nearly all sold capacity to be DCR.
Current EBITDA spreads on new orders said to be similar to FY26 levels.
IREDA term loan of INR 3,306 crore at 7.95%; about 75-80% expected to be drawn by March 2027, with 15-20% retention spilling into FY28.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex in cash flow about INR 650 crore; gross block rise of about INR 1,000 crore (adjusted for grant) mainly for Units 5 and 6 modules. Land acquisition of about INR 311 crore for the expansion was expensed this year per the Q&A.
Module line commissioning: 2.5 GW in May 2025 and 2.5 GW in Dec 2025 at Sulibele, Bengaluru.
Land at Devanahalli fully paid and in possession; construction started and module line order finalised.
Management cited that module lines typically reach 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, which is why module capacity is sized above cell capacity.
Cell capacity at 2.94 GW already built for G12 and line can switch from M10 to G12R through a kit change.
demand_pricing: DCR module price about INR 21-22/W; non-DCR module about INR 14-15/W. Management says DCR pricing is resilient and has not seen upward pressure despite limited domestic cell capacity.
Customer mix cited: IPPs about 40%, C&I about 30% (from prior analyst framing; not contradicted). Average top-10 customer order size rose to 221 MW from 121 MW.

Demand drivers cited: PM-KUSUM (KUSUM-C) and PM Surya Ghar for DCR; ALMM List-2 for cells expected to phase in, with utility projects bid after August 2025 covered; ALMM for IPP demand expected around FY28 or late 2027.

544609|2026-09.headline: Physicswallah Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR1,242 crores, a record, with Pre-Ind AS EBITDA of INR233 crores at an 18.8% margin.

Enterprise client count rose from 34 to 38; 28 net new clients added; top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue; client retention 95%. Management said top-5 concentration has declined.

Management said customers negotiate hard on managed-services and implementation pricing in India, while accepting AWS consumption costs. Hardware prices reportedly doubled or tripled, which management views as a tailwind for cloud migration.

544610|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 27.5% YoY to INR 95.21 crore; FY27 outlook raised to INR 202 crore from INR 190.56 crore.

PAT grew 32.4% to INR 12.03 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR 4.7 crore as receivables rose to INR 39.5 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue outlook to INR 202 crore, leaving a gap of under INR 8 crore to the INR 210 crore goal. International expansion (US subsidiary registered, Middle East and Singapore go-to-market recalibrated) was triggered.

544612|2026-03.headline: FY26 value added revenue rose 12.3% to INR49,180 million with a record 18.8% EBITDA margin; Q4 EBITDA up 17.6% to INR2,573 million.
544612|2026-03.overview: Management reported its best full year yet: FY26 VAR grew 12.3% to INR49,180 million, EBITDA rose 13.5% to INR9,255 million, and EBITDA margin reached a record 18.8% of VAR. Q4 VAR grew 17.5% to INR14,058 million, with EBITDA margin stable at 18.3% despite geopolitical cost pressures. Advanced Ride Technologies drove growth (FY26 up 19.7%), while Clean Air and Powertrain grew only 5.5% for the year. Lifetime order book stood at INR124,000 million at March 31, 2026, with exports and new Clean Air and bearings wins cited as growth drivers.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,296 million, up 5.5% YoY; Q4 INR6,905 million, up 9.9%. Growth tepid due to OEM and within-OEM mix shifts (lower-end SUVs, EV mix at a European OEM), not share loss per management.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,885 million, up 19.7% YoY; Q4 INR7,153 million, up 26%. DCx DaVinci mechanical suspension adopted by a leading Indian OEM for a flagship SUV.

guidance_outlook: Lifetime order book of INR124,000 million gives 100% visibility of FY2028 internal revenue target; management expects double-digit medium-term growth.
Export order book expected to keep growing; current exports are about 5-6% of sales versus a 14-20% share of the order book (as stated).
New West India shock absorber plant (board-approved) expected to take 6-12 months to commission; peak revenue contribution expected mid-2028 to 2029.
Clean Air entry into the largest Indian PV OEM's supplier panel for a Gasoline Particulate Filter; growth expected from late FY27/FY28.
Management expects margins to remain stable going forward.

Capex-to-steady-state revenue ratio cited as roughly 1:3.
Localization about 89-90%, management intends to keep it near 90% over the long term.
demand_pricing: Management says the DCx DaVinci suspension has 3-4 OEMs interested, including Indian, Japanese, Korean and European OEMs; it targets about 50% of India's roughly 5-5.5 million PV market.
Conventional mechanical dampers still dominate over 90% of Indian passenger vehicles.
Export drivers cited: technology equalization (BS6.2 with RDE, Euro 6 RDE), China-plus-one sourcing, labour cost advantage and rupee depreciation.

Direct material cost (steel) recovered through quarterly escalator agreements; indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, fuel) being recovered through customer negotiations, which management says can be tough.
Management said currency depreciation gives an immediate 15-20% improvement in global competitiveness.

qa_highlights.question: How will exports ramp over the next two to three years, and when will the new plants and bearings orders commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are described as middle-ended, with a critical mass around 2028 and ramp starting 2027-28. The West India plant takes 6-12 months to commission; peak around mid-2028 to 2029. Bearings value not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is content per vehicle for commercial vehicle exhaust systems versus passenger vehicles, and how do diesel, petrol, CNG and hybrid differ?
qa_highlights.answer: A commercial exhaust is 3-4x a passenger car system and can reach 10x for tractors with aftertreatment. Diesel carries higher hot-end content. Hybrids can lift content from 1x to 1.5-2x. CNG and hybrid need exhaust systems with no content loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports go directly to third-party OEMs or only to Tenneco group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports go both to Tenneco group entities and to third-party OEMs with group permission, which management frames as partnership, not competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why no two-wheeler suspension or Clean Air two-wheeler presence, and is the CV localization point about Clean Air?
qa_highlights.answer: Management avoids low-margin two- and three-wheelers and will enter only with technology differentiation; M&A also being considered. The CV localization reference relates to Clean Air, with localization about 89-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Clean Air growth tepid and what drives the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was held back by absence from the largest PV OEM and by mix shifts at existing OEMs. Margins attributed to the P3 operating model, standardized Lego-brick product design, and a higher-margin export order book; management expects margins to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: How do OEMs upgrade from passive to passive-plus or DaVinci suspension, and what is the cost delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Upgrades within mechanical suspension fit the existing packaging envelope with small cost delta. Electronics and software (semi-active CVSA) above about INR35 lakh MSRP need routing and ECU changes, which raise cost substantially.

qa_highlights.question: How are currency movements and indirect cost inflation handled in export contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Currency depreciation is seen as a benefit. Indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, LPG, CNG, crude) are being bundled and recovered from customers, with cost-cutting in SG&A and factory efficiency as mitigation.

544619|2026-09.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR196.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 37.2%, a record quarter despite Fortified Rice pause.
544619|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with revenue up 21% YoY and 24% QoQ, and EBITDA margin up about 310 bps YoY to 37.2%. Pharma Food Nutrition (PFN) drove growth, rising 57% YoY, while Specialty Ingredients fell 25% YoY after the Government's Fortified Rice programme paused. PAT grew only 11% YoY to INR51.8 crore because of lower other income, a higher effective tax rate of 27%, and new greenfield depreciation. Management guided to positive YoY growth in Specialty Ingredients in Q3 and Q4 and kept the Dahej battery-materials start date of April 2027.
